name: Yule: Return of the Light
description: A solstice spread for the longest night, when the old sun dies and the new one is reborn. It honors what the dark half of the year has taught you and kindles a small flame of hope to carry toward spring.

positions.name: The Longest Night
positions.meaning: What the darkness of this past season has asked of you; the hardship or stillness you have endured.
positions.guide: Honour the dark you have come through. What did this past season ask you to endure, and how does this card reflect it?

positions.name: Gift of the Dark
positions.meaning: The wisdom, rest or hidden strength you gained while the light was low.
positions.guide: Even the longest night leaves something behind. What wisdom or rest did you gain while the light was low?

positions.name: What to Leave in the Old Year
positions.meaning: The habit, fear or burden to let die with the old sun.
positions.guide: Imagine setting this card on the dying embers of the old sun. Which burden or fear are you ready to let go with it?

positions.name: The Newborn Sun
positions.meaning: The fresh hope or seed of light being born in you now.
positions.guide: Look for the smallest glimmer in this card. What fresh hope is being born in you on this longest night?

positions.name: Light to Carry Forward
positions.meaning: How to tend that small flame through the rest of winter.
positions.guide: Cup your hands as if around a candle. What daily act of care will keep this new flame alive until spring?

howToUse: Read on the solstice night by a single candle, ideally after a moment of sitting in full darkness. Lay the first three cards in a low row, then the newborn sun card centered above them and the final card at the top, like a flame rising. Read the bottom row as the closing of the old year and the upper cards as the returning light. Keep the top card on your altar until Imbolc.
intention: In the longest night I honor the dark and welcome the returning sun. Show me what to release and what light to carry.
bestTime: Winter Solstice / Yule (Dec 20–23), or any night in December

name: Imbolc: First Stirrings
description: A gentle spread for Brigid's festival, when the first lambs are born and the earth quickens beneath the snow. It reveals the seeds already stirring in your life and how to nurture them with Brigid's gifts of hearth, healing and inspiration.

positions.name: Beneath the Snow
positions.meaning: The dream or project quietly stirring under the surface of your life.
positions.guide: Picture this card sleeping under snow. What quiet dream have you been keeping warm through the winter months?

positions.name: Brigid's Flame
positions.meaning: The inspiration or creative fire available to you now.
positions.guide: Imagine Brigid's flame flickering in this card. Where does it light up your creativity, and what wants to be made?

positions.name: The Healing Well
positions.meaning: What needs cleansing or healing before new growth can begin.
positions.guide: Dip your hands into the well with this card. What old hurt or heaviness needs washing before you can begin?

positions.name: First Green Shoot
positions.meaning: The first small, practical step that lets the seed break through.
positions.guide: Look for the smallest, greenest thing in this card. What one simple step could you take before the week is out?

howToUse: Sweep your space and light a white candle for Brigid before reading. Lay the four cards in a row from left to right, like the earth waking from winter. Pay attention to Aces, Pages and the suit of Wands, which often mark new beginnings at this season. Write the final card's advice on a strip of cloth or paper and tie it near your door as a Brigid's ribbon.
intention: Brigid of the flame and the well, show me what is waking within me and how to tend it.
bestTime: Imbolc (Feb 1–2), late winter (late Jan–Feb)

name: Ostara: Balance and Bloom
description: A spring equinox spread built on the moment day and night stand equal. Two pairs of cards weigh light against dark and then reveal what is ready to blossom as the light begins to win.

positions.name: Light in Balance
positions.meaning: What is thriving and well-supported in your life right now.
positions.guide: Look for the sunlight in this card. What in your life is thriving right now, and who or what is helping it grow?

positions.name: Dark in Balance
positions.meaning: What still needs rest, patience or attention in the shadows.
positions.guide: Let your eyes rest in the card's shadows. What part of you still needs rest or patience before it is ready?

positions.name: The Egg
positions.meaning: The potential waiting to hatch: a plan, relationship or self you are growing into.
positions.guide: Imagine cupping this card like a warm egg. What plan, bond or self is quietly growing inside, waiting for its moment?

positions.name: First Blossom
positions.meaning: How that potential begins to bloom over the coming season.
positions.guide: Picture the first green shoots of spring opening in this card. What small, real sign of blooming could you look for this season?

howToUse: Read at the equinox, ideally at sunrise or sunset. Lay the first two cards side by side as the balance, then the egg and blossom cards in a row beneath them. Compare the top pair for equilibrium: if one card feels much heavier, that area of life needs rebalancing before the bottom row can flourish. Plant a seed or decorate an egg with a symbol from the last card.
intention: As day and night stand equal, show me my balance and the bloom that waits within me.
bestTime: Spring Equinox / Ostara (Mar 19–22), early spring (Mar–Apr)

name: Beltane: Fire and Flower
description: A May Eve spread of passion, union and vitality, laid in the shape of a maypole. It explores desire, creative fire and the joyful partnerships that make life fertile.

positions.name: The Maypole
positions.meaning: The central desire or passion rooting you to the earth this season.
positions.guide: Stand tall like the maypole. What desire does this card show rooting you to the earth and lifting you skyward this season?

positions.name: The Bonfire
positions.meaning: What to leap through: the fear or hesitation to burn away.
positions.guide: Picture the bonfire in front of you. What fear or hesitation in this card are you ready to leap over and burn away?

positions.name: The Flower Crown
positions.meaning: The beauty, pleasure or joy asking to be celebrated.
positions.guide: Let yourself smile at this card. What beauty or pleasure in your life is asking to be crowned and celebrated?

positions.name: The Ribbon Dance
positions.meaning: The partnership, collaboration or union that weaves your life together.
positions.guide: Think of the ribbons weaving round the pole. Who in your life does this card show you dancing with, in love, friendship or work?

positions.name: The Greenwood Blessing
positions.meaning: What will grow from honoring your passion: the fruit of the season.
positions.guide: Imagine the greenwood heavy with fruit. If you honour your passion, what does this card say will grow from it?

howToUse: Read outdoors or beside a fire if you can, with fresh flowers nearby. Place the maypole card in the center, the bonfire card above, the flower crown to the left, the ribbon dance to the right and the blessing below. Read the outer four cards as the energies circling your central desire. Cups and Wands here speak strongly of love and creative heat.
intention: By fire and flower, show me what I desire, what I must leap through, and what will bloom.
bestTime: Beltane / May Eve (Apr 30–May 1), late spring (May)

name: Litha: Height of the Sun
description: A midsummer spread laid as a radiant sun: one central card ringed by six rays. At the peak of the light it shows where you shine, what you have achieved and how to make the most of the long bright days before the wheel turns toward harvest.

positions.name: Ray of Strength
positions.meaning: Where your power and confidence are strongest right now.
positions.guide: Stand tall as you look at this card. Where in your life do you feel most sure of your own power right now?

positions.name: Ray of Achievement
positions.meaning: What you have accomplished since the dark of the year.
positions.guide: Think back to the darkest days of winter. What has grown since then that this card helps you see and celebrate?

positions.name: Ray of Joy
positions.meaning: What brings you warmth and delight; how to have more of it.
positions.guide: Let this card warm you like sunlight on skin. What delights you here, and how could you invite more of it in?

positions.name: Ray of Shadow
positions.meaning: What the bright light reveals that you would rather not see.
positions.guide: Bright light casts sharp shadows. Gently ask what this card shows you that you would prefer not to see.

positions.name: Ray of Abundance
positions.meaning: What is ripening and will soon be ready to harvest.
positions.guide: Look at this card like a ripening field. What in your life is almost ready to be gathered in?

positions.name: Ray of Turning
positions.meaning: What to prepare as the days begin to shorten again.
positions.guide: The wheel is already turning toward harvest. What does this card suggest you prepare while the days are still long?

positions.name: The Midsummer Sun
positions.meaning: The heart of the reading: your own inner sun and how it wants to shine.
positions.guide: Close your eyes and feel a sun glowing in your chest. How does this card want that inner light to shine?

howToUse: Read at noon on the solstice or in the long evening light. Lay the six rays clockwise from the top in a circle, then place the central sun card last. Read the rays in order, then interpret the center as the force that unites them. The Sun, Strength and the suit of Wands appearing here are especially blessed.
intention: At the height of the sun, show me where I shine and how to carry this light through the turning year.
bestTime: Summer Solstice / Litha (Jun 20–22), midsummer (Jun–Jul)

name: Lammas: First Harvest
description: A Lughnasadh spread for the first grain harvest, when the first loaf is baked and thanks are given. It counts what your efforts have yielded, what must be sacrificed for the harvest to continue and what to save as seed for next year.

positions.name: The First Sheaf
positions.meaning: The first fruit of your labors this year; what has already come in.
positions.guide: Count your blessings like sheaves of grain. What has already come in from your hard work this year that you have not fully noticed?

positions.name: The Sickle
positions.meaning: What must be cut away or sacrificed so the harvest can be gathered.
positions.guide: Every harvest needs a blade. What does this card say must be cut away so you can gather what is ripe?

positions.name: The Loaf
positions.meaning: What to share, celebrate or give thanks for.
positions.guide: Imagine breaking bread with people you love. What in this card deserves to be shared, celebrated or thanked?

positions.name: The Remaining Field
positions.meaning: The work still ripening that needs more time and effort.
positions.guide: Walk the rows still standing. What work in this card needs more time and tending before it is ready?

positions.name: Seed for Next Year
positions.meaning: What to save and carry forward as the seed of future growth.
positions.guide: Hold this card like a handful of seed. What lesson or hope will you save and plant again next year?

howToUse: Bake or buy a loaf of bread and set it beside your deck. Lay the five cards in a gentle arch from left to right, like a sheaf bending in the wind. Pentacles here speak directly of earned rewards. After reading, break the bread and leave the first piece outside as an offering of thanks.
intention: At the first harvest I give thanks. Show me what I have reaped and what I must sow again.
bestTime: Lammas / Lughnasadh (Jul 31–Aug 2), late summer (Aug)

name: Mabon: Second Harvest
description: An autumn equinox spread of gratitude and balance. As day and night stand equal once more, it weighs your gains and losses and prepares you to descend gracefully into the dark half of the year.

positions.name: What I Have Gathered
positions.meaning: The blessings, lessons and abundance this year has given you.
positions.guide: Gather your thanks. What blessings and lessons from this year does this card bring to mind? Name at least one aloud.

positions.name: What I Have Lost
positions.meaning: What has fallen away, and the peace to be found in letting it go.
positions.guide: Day and night stand equal now. Look at what this card shows falling away, and ask where peace might be found in its leaving.

positions.name: Storing for Winter
positions.meaning: What to preserve and protect as the nights grow long.
positions.guide: Imagine filling your larder for winter. What in this card is worth preserving and protecting as the nights grow long?

positions.name: Into the Dark
positions.meaning: The inner work and rest awaiting you in the coming season.
positions.guide: Feel the year beginning its descent. What quiet inner work or rest does this card invite you into?

howToUse: Set apples, gourds or autumn leaves on your altar. Lay the first two cards side by side as the scales of the equinox, then the two lower cards beneath them. Read the top pair for the balance of gain and loss, and the lower pair as guidance for the descent into winter. Write three things you are grateful for after the reading.
intention: At the turning of the year I give thanks and find my balance. Show me what to keep and what to release.
bestTime: Autumn Equinox / Mabon (Sep 21–23), early autumn (Sep–Oct)

name: Yes or No: Two Paths
description: A quick two-card spread for yes-or-no questions that does not reduce the tarot to a coin toss. Instead of one blunt answer, it shows what unfolds if you say yes and what unfolds if you say no, so you choose with open eyes.

positions.name: If Yes
positions.meaning: What happens, or what you experience, if you say yes or take this step.
positions.guide: Imagine saying yes out loud and step into this card. How does your body react: lighter, tighter, excited, afraid?

positions.name: If No
positions.meaning: What happens, or what you experience, if you say no or hold back.
positions.guide: Now imagine saying no and step into this card instead. Is there relief here, or a quiet sense of something missed?

howToUse: Phrase your question so it can be answered yes or no, then shuffle while holding it in mind. Lay the two cards side by side. Compare them honestly: which outcome feels more nourishing, more aligned, more alive? As a simple rule of thumb, bright and flowing cards (the Sun, the Star, aces, many Cups) lean toward a happy result, while heavy or blocked cards (the Tower, many Swords) urge caution. The choice remains yours.
intention: Show me both paths clearly, so that I may choose the one that serves my highest good.
bestTime: Any time of year, whenever a decision is pressing

name: Obstacle Spread
description: A five-card spread for when you feel stuck. It names the obstacle, uncovers its root, and reveals both the hidden help and the action that will move you past it.

positions.name: The Situation
positions.meaning: Where you stand and what you are trying to achieve.
positions.guide: Start by naming it plainly. What are you trying to reach, and where does this card show you standing right now?

positions.name: The Obstacle
positions.meaning: What is blocking your way right now.
positions.guide: Look straight at what blocks you. What in this card feels like the wall, and how big is it really?

positions.name: The Root
positions.meaning: Where the obstacle truly comes from: inside you, in others or in circumstance.
positions.guide: Dig beneath the block. Does this card point to something inside you, in someone else, or simply in circumstance?

positions.name: Hidden Help
positions.meaning: An ally, resource or strength you have overlooked.
positions.guide: Look at the edges and background of this card. What ally or strength have you been walking right past?

positions.name: The Way Through
positions.meaning: The action or shift in perspective that clears the path.
positions.guide: Imagine yourself already on the other side. What one action or change of view does this card suggest to get you there?

howToUse: Lay the situation card on the left and the obstacle card directly to its right, as if standing in the way. Place the root beneath the obstacle and hidden help above it, then the way through on the far right. Read left to right as a journey: you, the wall, and what lies beyond it. If the way-through card is unclear, draw one clarifier and lay it beside it.
intention: Show me what stands in my way, where it comes from, and how I may pass.
bestTime: Any time of year; especially helpful at the turn of a season

name: Healing Spread
description: A compassionate spread for any wound of body, heart or spirit. It does not replace medical care; it helps you understand what is asking for healing and how to support your own recovery.

positions.name: The Wound
positions.meaning: What is hurting and asking for attention.
positions.guide: Be very gentle here. Look at this card and simply name what hurts, without needing to fix it yet.

positions.name: The Lesson
positions.meaning: What this pain is teaching you or asking you to understand.
positions.guide: Pain can be a teacher. What is this card trying to help you understand about yourself or your needs?

positions.name: What to Release
positions.meaning: The belief, habit or memory that keeps the wound open.
positions.guide: Breathe out slowly. What belief or habit in this card keeps the wound open, and are you ready to set it down?

positions.name: Medicine
positions.meaning: What nourishes and restores you: a practice, person or change.
positions.guide: Look for what nourishes in this card. Is your medicine a practice, a person, or a change you have been putting off?

positions.name: Healed Self
positions.meaning: Who you are becoming as you heal.
positions.guide: Picture yourself a season from now, healing well. Does this card show who you are becoming, and can you welcome them?

howToUse: Hold a piece of Rose Quartz or a cup of warm herbal tea while you shuffle. Lay the wound card at the bottom center, the lesson and release cards to its upper left and upper right, the medicine card above, and the healed self at the top. Read upward from the wound to wholeness. Be gentle with yourself; difficult cards here simply show where care is needed. For physical concerns, always see a qualified healthcare provider.
intention: Show me with kindness where I am hurting and how I may heal.
bestTime: Any time of year; late winter and spring for renewal

name: Money & Abundance
description: A practical prosperity spread that looks at money honestly: what you have, how it flows, what blocks it and where new abundance can come from. It is grounding rather than wishful, pairing magic with real action.

positions.name: Current Finances
positions.meaning: The true state of your money and resources right now.
positions.guide: Take a steady breath and look without flinching. What does this card say about your money as it truly is, not as you fear or wish?

positions.name: Money Beliefs
positions.meaning: The beliefs or family patterns shaping how you earn, spend and save.
positions.guide: Listen for an old family saying about money as you look. Which belief does this card echo, and is it really yours?

positions.name: What Drains
positions.meaning: Where money or energy is leaking away.
positions.guide: Look for anything spilling, broken or wasted in this card. Where is money or energy leaking out of your days?

positions.name: What Grows
positions.meaning: Where your resources are already multiplying and could be nurtured.
positions.guide: Find what is flourishing in this card. Which resource of yours is already multiplying, and how could you tend it?

positions.name: New Opportunity
positions.meaning: A new source of income, skill or opening to watch for.
positions.guide: Scan this card for a figure, path or tool you had not expected. What new skill, contact or income stream might it point to?

positions.name: Abundant Action
positions.meaning: The concrete step to take this month to invite prosperity.
positions.guide: Make it practical. What is one concrete step this card suggests you take before the month is out?

howToUse: Place a coin or a sprig of Basil on your table. Lay the cards in two rows of three: the top row (current finances, beliefs, drains) shows where you stand, and the bottom row (grows, opportunity, action) shows the way forward. Watch for Pentacles and how they interact with other suits. Commit to the action card in a real, practical way within seven days.
intention: Show me the truth of my resources and the path to steady, lasting abundance.
bestTime: Any time of year; especially harvest season (Aug–Sep) and the start of a new year

name: Creativity: Calling the Muse
description: A spread for artists, writers and makers of every kind. It helps you understand your creative well, unblock stalled projects and hear what your muse is trying to bring through.

positions.name: The Creative Well
positions.meaning: The state of your creative energy right now.
positions.guide: Lower an imaginary bucket into your creative well. Does this card bring it up full, half-empty or muddy today?

positions.name: The Block
positions.meaning: What is dampening your inspiration or stopping you from beginning.
positions.guide: Be curious rather than critical. What in this card mirrors the thing that stops you before you begin?

positions.name: The Muse Speaks
positions.meaning: The idea, image or theme that wants to be expressed.
positions.guide: Let your eyes wander the card's images and colours. Which detail catches you? That might be what your muse wants made.

positions.name: The Craft
positions.meaning: The skill or discipline to develop to bring it to life.
positions.guide: Think of the hands that make things. What skill or practice does this card ask you to sharpen, a little each day?

positions.name: The Work Revealed
positions.meaning: What your creation may become if you honor the muse.
positions.guide: Picture the finished piece. If you trust the muse, what might your work become, according to this card?

howToUse: Read near your workspace, perhaps with a lit orange or yellow candle. Lay the five cards in a V shape: the well at the bottom point, the block and the muse rising on the left, the craft and the finished work rising on the right. Let the images spark free association; write or sketch for ten minutes immediately afterward without editing.
intention: Muse of my heart, show me what wants to be made and how I may bring it into the world.
bestTime: Any time of year; spring and Imbolc for fresh inspiration

name: Meeting Your Spirit Guide
description: A four-card spread for contacting the guides, allies and helping spirits who walk with you. It reveals something of their nature, their message and how to strengthen the connection.

positions.name: Who Walks With Me
positions.meaning: The nature or quality of the guide drawing near.
positions.guide: Sit still and sense who draws near. Is the presence in this card fierce, tender, playful or wise?

positions.name: Their Message
positions.meaning: What your guide most wants you to know right now.
positions.guide: Listen as if a friend is leaning close to whisper. What is the simplest message this card carries for you today?

positions.name: How They Speak
positions.meaning: The signs, dreams or symbols through which they reach you.
positions.guide: Notice the symbols in this card: animals, colours, objects. Have any of them crossed your path or your dreams lately?

positions.name: Deepening the Bond
positions.meaning: A practice or offering that strengthens your connection.
positions.guide: What small offering or practice does this card suggest? A candle, a walk, a moment of thanks each night could be enough.

howToUse: Cast a circle or simply ground and center, then meditate for a few minutes inviting only helpful, loving guides to come forward. Lay the first card at the top, the message and how-they-speak cards side by side below it, and the bond card at the bottom, forming a diamond. Court cards often describe the guide's personality; Major Arcana suggest a powerful or long-standing ally. Thank your guide aloud when finished.
intention: I call only to those guides who come in love and for my highest good. Show yourself to me and share your message.
bestTime: Autumn into winter (Oct–Dec), especially around Samhain; any quiet night

name: Hecate's Crossroads
description: A spread dedicated to Hecate, keeper of the keys and goddess of the three-way crossroads. Where a simple decision spread weighs two options, this one opens three paths and lets you see the gift and the cost of each before her torchlight.

positions.name: Where I Stand
positions.meaning: You at the crossroads: your situation and state of mind.
positions.guide: Stand still at the meeting of three roads. How does this card show you right now: calm, torn, tired or eager?

positions.name: Hecate's Torch
positions.meaning: The light Hecate offers: the insight you most need to choose well.
positions.guide: Imagine Hecate raising her torch over this card. What does her light reveal that you most need to see before choosing?

positions.name: First Path: The Road
positions.meaning: Where the first option leads.
positions.guide: Walk the first road in your mind as you study this card. Where does it take you, and how do you feel when you arrive?

positions.name: First Path: The Price
positions.meaning: What the first option asks of you or costs.
positions.guide: Nothing at the crossroads is free. What does this card say the first path will ask you to give up or carry?

positions.name: Second Path: The Road
positions.meaning: Where the second option leads.
positions.guide: Turn toward the second road and let this card unfold ahead of you. Which part of it tugs at you, and which makes you hesitate?

positions.name: Second Path: The Price
positions.meaning: What the second option asks of you or costs.
positions.guide: Weigh the cost honestly. Is the price in this card one you could pay with an open heart?

positions.name: Third Path: The Road
positions.meaning: Where the third option leads, often the one not yet considered.
positions.guide: This may be the road you had not thought of. What surprises you in this card, and why might you have overlooked it?

positions.name: Third Path: The Price
positions.meaning: What the third option asks of you or costs.
positions.guide: Look closely at what the third path demands. Compare it with the other two prices: is it lighter, heavier or simply different?

positions.name: Hecate's Key
positions.meaning: The key that unlocks the right choice; advice for walking any path.
positions.guide: Picture Hecate placing this key in your palm. What door does it open, and how will it help you walk whichever road you choose?

howToUse: Read at night, ideally at a crossroads or with three candles lit, and leave an offering such as garlic, bread or honey. Lay where-I-stand at the bottom center and Hecate's torch above it. Then fan out three paths: the first rising to the upper left, the second straight up and the third to the upper right, each with its road card and its price card beyond. Place the key at the very bottom. Name the options before drawing, or leave the third path unnamed so the cards can reveal it.
intention: Hecate, lady of the crossroads, light my way. Show me each road and its price, and grant me the key to choose.
bestTime: Hecate's Night (Nov 16), Samhain season (Oct–Nov), or any dark night of the year

name: Triple Goddess
description: A spread honoring the Maiden, Mother and Crone, the three faces of the Goddess and of the moon. Each card speaks with one of her voices, and a fourth card shows how they unite in you.

positions.name: The Maiden
positions.meaning: Waxing moon. What is new, curious and beginning in you; the potential to embrace.
positions.guide: Meet the Maiden with curiosity. What new beginning in this card makes you feel young, eager, or a little nervous?

positions.name: The Mother
positions.meaning: Full moon. What you are nurturing, creating and bringing to fullness.
positions.guide: The Mother holds the full moon in her arms. What are you nurturing, and does this card show it coming to fullness?

positions.name: The Crone
positions.meaning: Waning moon. The wisdom of endings; what to let go and what you already know deep down.
positions.guide: Sit with the Crone and her quiet knowing. What does this card ask you to release, and what do you already know deep down?

positions.name: The Goddess Within
positions.meaning: How all three faces unite in you now; the guidance of the whole moon.
positions.guide: Imagine all three faces gathered in you. How does this card weave beginning, fullness and ending into one guidance?

howToUse: Lay the Maiden on the left, the Mother in the center and the Crone on the right, echoing the waxing, full and waning moon symbol. Place the Goddess Within card beneath the Mother. Read each card in the voice of that aspect, then read the bottom card as their combined counsel. The High Priestess, Empress and Moon appearing here are especially significant.
intention: Maiden, Mother and Crone, speak to me with your three voices and show me the Goddess within.
bestTime: Any time of year; Beltane (Maiden), Lammas (Mother) and Samhain (Crone) are especially potent

name: Birthday: Solar Return
description: A personal new-year spread to read on or near your birthday, when the sun returns to the place it held when you were born. It reviews the year behind you and sets the theme, gifts and challenges of your coming year.

positions.name: The Year Behind
positions.meaning: The main theme or lesson of the year just ending.
positions.guide: Look back over the past twelve months. What lesson or theme does this card sum up about the year just ending?

positions.name: What I Outgrew
positions.meaning: What you can lovingly leave behind as you turn a new age.
positions.guide: Like a coat that no longer fits, what in this card can you lovingly leave behind as you turn a new age?

positions.name: The Birthday Self
positions.meaning: Who you are now, at the beginning of this new solar year.
positions.guide: Meet yourself on this birthday. Do you recognise who you are now in this card, or someone you are stepping into?

positions.name: Theme of the Year
positions.meaning: The central energy or story of your coming year.
positions.guide: Imagine this card as the title of your coming year's story. What chapters do you see unfolding beneath it?

positions.name: Gift of the Year
positions.meaning: A blessing, talent or opportunity the year will bring.
positions.guide: Open your hands to receive. What gift or opportunity in this card would you love to say yes to this year?

positions.name: Challenge of the Year
positions.meaning: The lesson or test to prepare for.
positions.guide: Every year brings a test. What does this card ask you to prepare for, and what will help you meet it?

positions.name: Birthday Wish
positions.meaning: The wish the universe supports; what to blow your candles out for.
positions.guide: Close your eyes as if before your birthday candles. What wish does this card say the universe will gladly support?

howToUse: Read on your birthday or within the week around it. Lay the first two cards on the left as the past, the birthday self in the center, and the theme, gift and challenge cards in a column on the right as the year ahead. Place the wish card above the birthday self. Make your birthday wish with the last card in mind, and revisit the reading on your next birthday.
intention: As the sun returns to my birth, show me the year I leave and the year I enter.
bestTime: On or within a week of your birthday, any time of year

name: Month Ahead by Moon Phases
description: A lunar calendar spread that lays one card for each of the eight phases of the coming moon cycle. Read it at the New Moon to see how the month will unfold and when to begin, push, celebrate, release and rest.

positions.name: New Moon
positions.meaning: The seed of the month: the intention to plant now.
positions.guide: In the dark of the new moon, hold this card like a seed. What intention do you want to plant for the month?

positions.name: Waxing Crescent
positions.meaning: The first steps and early support as the intention takes root.
positions.guide: A thin crescent appears. What first step or helping hand does this card show as your intention takes root?

positions.name: First Quarter
positions.meaning: The challenge or decision point that tests your commitment.
positions.guide: At the half moon comes a test. What choice in this card will ask you to prove how much you want this?

positions.name: Waxing Gibbous
positions.meaning: What to refine, adjust and keep working on.
positions.guide: The moon is nearly full. What in this card needs tweaking, polishing or a little more patience?

positions.name: Full Moon
positions.meaning: What comes to fullness, is revealed or celebrated.
positions.guide: Bathe this card in full moonlight. What comes to fullness or is revealed, and how will you celebrate it?

positions.name: Waning Gibbous
positions.meaning: What to share, teach or give thanks for.
positions.guide: As the light begins to wane, what does this card invite you to share, teach, or give thanks for?

positions.name: Last Quarter
positions.meaning: What to release, forgive or clear away.
positions.guide: Breathe out with the half moon. What does this card ask you to forgive, clear away or finally let go?

positions.name: Waning Crescent
positions.meaning: How to rest, reflect and prepare for the next cycle.
positions.guide: In the last sliver of light, slow down. How does this card suggest you rest and ready yourself for the next cycle?

howToUse: Read on or just after the New Moon. Lay the eight cards in a circle beginning at the top and moving clockwise, following the moon around its cycle. Read each card when its phase arrives as well as all together at the start. Mark the phase dates in a calendar beside each card, and journal at each phase to see how the reading unfolds.
intention: Moon of the coming month, show me your path through each phase, from seed to rest.
bestTime: Any month of the year, read at the start of a lunar cycle

name: Inner Child
description: A tender spread for reconnecting with the child you once were. It reveals old hurts that still echo, the joys that were set aside, and how to become the loving guardian your younger self needed.

positions.name: My Inner Child
positions.meaning: How your inner child feels and appears to you today.
positions.guide: Picture yourself at seven or eight years old looking at this card with you. How do they feel, and how do they want to be seen?

positions.name: The Old Hurt
positions.meaning: A wound from childhood that still shapes you.
positions.guide: Go gently. What childhood hurt does this card stir, and where do you still feel it showing up in your life today?

positions.name: The Lost Joy
positions.meaning: A delight, game or dream your younger self loved and you set aside.
positions.guide: Remember a game or dream you loved when you were small. Does this card remind you of it, and could you bring it back?

positions.name: What They Need
positions.meaning: What your inner child needs from you now to feel safe and loved.
positions.guide: Ask your younger self quietly what they need to feel safe. Let this card answer, even if the answer is simple.

positions.name: The Loving Guardian
positions.meaning: How to care for and reparent yourself going forward.
positions.guide: Imagine yourself as the grown-up you once needed. What does this card show you doing to care for that child now?

howToUse: Make the space cozy: a blanket, a childhood photo, perhaps something sweet. Lay the inner child card in the center, the old hurt to the left, the lost joy to the right, what they need below and the loving guardian above, so the guardian watches over the child. Speak to your inner child aloud as you read. Pages and the Six of Cups often appear in this spread with special warmth. If deep trauma surfaces, consider support from a counselor.
intention: Little one within me, I am listening. Show me what you need and how I can care for you.
bestTime: Any time of year; spring and summer for play, autumn for healing work

name: New Love & Soulmate
description: A spread for those seeking love, or wondering about a new connection. It looks at your readiness, what you truly want and the qualities of the love that is drawing near, without promising names or dates.

positions.name: My Heart Now
positions.meaning: Your readiness for love and the state of your heart.
positions.guide: Place a hand over your heart. Does this card show a heart that feels open and ready, or one still healing?

positions.name: What I Truly Desire
positions.meaning: The kind of love and partnership your soul is seeking.
positions.guide: Set aside what you think you should want. What kind of love does this card say your soul is truly seeking?

positions.name: What Blocks Love
positions.meaning: A fear, pattern or belief keeping love at a distance.
positions.guide: Be gentle with what you find. What fear or old pattern in this card might be keeping love at arm's length?

positions.name: The Love Approaching
positions.meaning: The qualities of the person or connection coming toward you.
positions.guide: Rather than a name or a face, notice qualities. What warmth, energy or character does this card bring toward you?

positions.name: Where We Meet
positions.meaning: The setting, activity or path that brings you together.
positions.guide: Look at the setting in this card. What place, activity or path might lead you across love's way?

positions.name: How to Open the Door
positions.meaning: The step that makes room for love to arrive.
positions.guide: Imagine your hand on the doorknob. What small step does this card suggest to make room for love to arrive?

howToUse: Light a pink or red candle and place a Rose Quartz or rose petals near your deck. Lay the cards in a heart shape: the first two at the top lobes, the next two below them, the meeting card nestled in the center between them, and the door card at the point. Read the left side as you and the right as the love approaching. Court cards in this spread often describe a person; the Lovers and Two of Cups are especially promising.
intention: Show me my heart, the love I seek, and how to open the door for it to find me.
bestTime: Spring into summer, Ostara to Litha (Mar–Jun), especially Beltane; or any Friday

name: Breakup Healing
description: A gentle spread for the end of a relationship. It helps you grieve honestly, understand what happened without blame, take your power back and open slowly to the future.

positions.name: What Ended
positions.meaning: The truth of what this relationship was and why it ended.
positions.guide: Look at this card without looking for someone to blame. What was this relationship truly, and what does the card say about why it ended?

positions.name: What I Grieve
positions.meaning: The loss that hurts most and deserves to be mourned.
positions.guide: Let yourself feel it. What loss in this card aches the most, and can you give it a moment of honest grief?

positions.name: The Lesson
positions.meaning: What this relationship taught you about love and yourself.
positions.guide: Think of who you were before and who you are now. What has this card got to teach you about love and about yourself?

positions.name: Reclaiming My Power
positions.meaning: The part of yourself to call back and strengthen.
positions.guide: Sit up a little straighter as you look. What part of yourself did you set aside, and how is this card calling it home?

positions.name: The Open Road
positions.meaning: What lies ahead as your heart heals.
positions.guide: Let this card be a window, not a promise. What hopeful thing do you see on the road ahead as your heart mends?

howToUse: Read when you feel ready, with tissues and a cup of Chamomile or Lemon Balm tea. Lay the five cards in a descending-then-rising line: what ended and what I grieve sloping down, the lesson at the low point, and reclaiming my power and the open road climbing up again. Let yourself feel the bottom card fully before moving upward. Repeat this spread a month later to see how far you have come.
intention: Help me grieve what was, learn what it taught me, and walk freely into what comes next.
bestTime: Any time of year; autumn and winter suit grieving, spring suits moving on

name: Moving House
description: A spread for anyone moving, or thinking of moving, to a new home. It honors the home you are leaving, explores the spirit of the new place, and advises on a smooth transition and a happy hearth.

positions.name: The Old Home
positions.meaning: What your current home has given you and how to say goodbye.
positions.guide: Walk through your old rooms in your mind. What has this home given you that this card helps you thank it for?

positions.name: What to Leave Behind
positions.meaning: Habits, clutter or energy that should not make the move.
positions.guide: Look at this card as you would a box marked 'do not pack'. What habit or energy should stay behind?

positions.name: The Journey
positions.meaning: How the move itself will go and what to watch for.
positions.guide: Picture the boxes, the van, the long day. What does this card advise you to watch for along the way?

positions.name: The Spirit of the New Home
positions.meaning: The character and energy of the new place and its land.
positions.guide: Imagine standing on the new doorstep and feeling the land beneath. What kind of spirit does this card say lives there?

positions.name: Blessing the Threshold
positions.meaning: How to cleanse, protect and claim the new space.
positions.guide: Think of salt, smoke, a sprig of rosemary at the door. How does this card suggest you cleanse and claim the space?

positions.name: Life in the New Home
positions.meaning: What awaits you once you settle in.
positions.guide: Picture a quiet evening once the boxes are gone. What does this card promise your life in the new home will hold?

howToUse: Lay the cards in the shape of a little house: the old home and what to leave behind side by side at the base, the journey and the spirit of the new home as the walls above, the threshold blessing beside them, and life in the new home as the roof peak. Read from the foundation up. Perform the threshold card's advice the day you get the keys, perhaps with salt, Rosemary and a new broom.
intention: Bless the home I leave and the home I go to. Show me how to make my new house a true home.
bestTime: Any time of year; spring and early summer are traditional moving seasons

name: Wheel of the Year
description: An eight-card year-ahead spread that follows the witch's Wheel of the Year rather than the calendar. Each card is laid at one of the eight sabbats, revealing the energy and lessons of every season as the wheel turns, with a ninth card at the hub.

positions.name: Samhain
positions.meaning: Endings, ancestors and what you are ready to let die. The witch's new year.
positions.guide: The witch's new year begins in the dark. What in this card are you ready to let die, and which ancestors might walk with you?

positions.name: Yule
positions.meaning: The return of the light: hope, rest and the small flame you will nurture through winter.
positions.guide: Picture a single candle on the longest night. What hope or rest does this card ask you to nurture through winter?

positions.name: Imbolc
positions.meaning: First stirrings: the seed or idea quietly waking and how to purify for new growth.
positions.guide: Feel the first stirring under frozen ground. What seed or idea is quietly waking in this card, and what needs clearing for it?

positions.name: Ostara
positions.meaning: Balance and blossoming: what begins to grow and flourish in spring.
positions.guide: Light and dark stand in balance at spring. What does this card show beginning to bud and flourish for you?

positions.name: Beltane
positions.meaning: Passion and union: love, creativity and the fire that drives you at the height of spring.
positions.guide: Feel the warmth of the Beltane fire. What love, creativity or passion does this card say will drive you at spring's height?

positions.name: Litha
positions.meaning: The peak of the sun: success, power and what will shine brightest.
positions.guide: Imagine the sun at its highest. Where does this card say you will shine brightest this year?

positions.name: Lammas
positions.meaning: First harvest: the early rewards of your work and what must be sacrificed.
positions.guide: The first sheaves are cut. What early reward does this card promise, and what might you need to give up for it?

positions.name: Mabon
positions.meaning: Second harvest: gratitude, balance and preparing for the descent into dark.
positions.guide: Pause in gratitude at the second harvest. What does this card ask you to give thanks for before the descent into dark?

positions.name: The Hub
positions.meaning: The heart of your whole year: the theme that turns the wheel.
positions.guide: Look at the centre of the wheel. How does this card's theme connect the eight seasons around it?

howToUse: Read at Samhain (the witch's new year) or at any sabbat, starting with the sabbat that comes next. Lay the eight cards in a circle clockwise from the top, beginning with Samhain, then place the hub card in the center. Read each card as the energy of the season around that sabbat. Return to the spread at each sabbat to reflect on how it has unfolded.
intention: As the great wheel turns, show me the gifts and lessons of each season of the year to come.
bestTime: Samhain (Oct 31–Nov 1), or any of the eight sabbats

name: Seven Planets
description: A spread built on the seven classical planets of traditional astrology and magic. Laid in a seven-pointed star, it surveys every major area of life under its planetary ruler, from the Sun's vitality to Saturn's lessons.

positions.name: Sun
positions.meaning: Vitality, identity and success. Where you shine and what gives you life.
positions.guide: Let the Sun warm this card. Where do you feel most alive and most yourself, and does this card show you shining or hiding?

positions.name: Moon
positions.meaning: Emotions, intuition and the home. What your inner tides are telling you.
positions.guide: Feel the Moon's tide in this card. What is your inner world whispering, and how does your home feel right now?

positions.name: Mars
positions.meaning: Courage, conflict and drive. Where to fight and where to stand down.
positions.guide: Look for the warrior's stance in this card. Which battle is worth your fire, and which one could you lay down?

positions.name: Mercury
positions.meaning: Thought, communication and travel. What to learn, say or study.
positions.guide: Let quick-footed Mercury read this card with you. Is there something to learn, a message to send or a journey to plan?

positions.name: Jupiter
positions.meaning: Growth, luck and abundance. Where blessings and expansion come from.
positions.guide: Jupiter opens wide hands. Where does this card show blessings arriving, and are you letting yourself receive them?

positions.name: Venus
positions.meaning: Love, beauty and pleasure. The state of your relationships and joys.
positions.guide: Look for beauty and pleasure in this card. How are your relationships and simple joys doing, and what would sweeten them?

positions.name: Saturn
positions.meaning: Limits, discipline and time. The lesson, responsibility or boundary to honor.
positions.guide: Saturn teaches through limits. What lesson, duty or boundary does this card ask you to honor patiently?

howToUse: Lay the seven cards in a circle clockwise from the top in the Chaldean order of the days of the week: Sun (Sunday), Moon (Monday), Mars (Tuesday), Mercury (Wednesday), Jupiter (Thursday), Venus (Friday) and Saturn (Saturday). Read each card in the light of its planet. For a week-long practice, revisit one card on its planetary day and work a small spell or meditation to that planet.
intention: By the seven wandering stars, show me the state of each realm of my life and how to bring them into harmony.
bestTime: Any time of year; begin on a Sunday

name: Mirror Spread
description: A spread of reflections laid in two facing columns. It compares how you see yourself with how others see you, and the face you show the world with the self you hide, revealing where your inner and outer images agree and where they diverge.

positions.name: How I See Myself
positions.meaning: Your own self-image right now.
positions.guide: Look at this card as if into a mirror. Do you like who you see, and is it kinder or harsher than the truth?

positions.name: How Others See Me
positions.meaning: The impression you make on those around you.
positions.guide: Think of a friend describing you to a stranger. Would they choose this card, and does that surprise you?

positions.name: The Face I Show
positions.meaning: The mask or persona you present to the world.
positions.guide: Notice the costume or pose in this card. What mask do you put on at work, online or in company?

positions.name: The Self I Hide
positions.meaning: What you keep behind the mask, from others or from yourself.
positions.guide: Breathe slowly and be tender. What are you keeping behind the mask, and who are you hiding it from?

positions.name: The Blind Spot
positions.meaning: What neither you nor others see clearly yet.
positions.guide: Look at the corners and background of this card. What small detail did you almost overlook, in the card and in yourself?

positions.name: The True Reflection
positions.meaning: The deeper truth that unites every image; who you truly are.
positions.guide: Lay this card beside the others. What thread runs through every reflection, the you that stays when the masks come off?

howToUse: Read in front of a mirror if possible, with a candle lit beside it. Lay the cards in two facing columns: the left column (1, 3, 5) is your inner view, and the right column (2, 4) is the outer view, with the true reflection set between the columns at the bottom. Compare each pair across the gap: similar cards show integrity, contrasting cards show where the image is distorted. Close by looking into your own eyes and speaking the true reflection card's message aloud.
intention: Mirror, show me true: how I am seen, how I see, and who I really am.
bestTime: Any time of year; autumn and winter suit inner reflection

name: Witch's Pyramid
description: A spread built on the Witch's Pyramid, the four powers of the Magus: To Know, To Will, To Dare and To Keep Silent, crowned by Spirit. It is ideal before working an important spell, testing whether each foundation of the magic is strong.

positions.name: To Know (Air)
positions.meaning: What you must understand about the situation and yourself before working magic.
positions.guide: Clear your mind like a cool breeze. What does this card say you must understand about the situation, or yourself, before you cast?

positions.name: To Will (Fire)
positions.meaning: The strength and clarity of your intent; where your will is focused or scattered.
positions.guide: Feel your intent as a flame. Is this card showing your will burning steady and focused, or flickering in many directions?

positions.name: To Dare (Water)
positions.meaning: The courage required; what you must be brave enough to feel, risk or act upon.
positions.guide: Water asks for courage. What feeling, risk or action does this card dare you to face for this working?

positions.name: To Keep Silent (Earth)
positions.meaning: What to hold privately and let gestate in quiet so its power is not spent.
positions.guide: Press your palms to the earth. What in this card should be kept private so its power can quietly grow?

positions.name: To Go (Spirit)
positions.meaning: The apex: how the four powers unite, and the likely outcome of your working.
positions.guide: Look at the four cards below as one foundation. Are they strong together, and what does this final card say your working will become?

howToUse: Read before casting an important spell or beginning a long magical undertaking. Lay the four foundation cards in a row as the base of the pyramid, from Air on the left to Earth on the right, then place the Spirit card above the center as the apex. Any weak or troubled base card shows which pillar to strengthen before you work. Keep this reading to yourself, honoring the power of silence.
intention: To know, to will, to dare, to keep silent. Show me the strength of each foundation and the shape of the magic they will raise.
bestTime: Any time of year, before a major spell or initiation

name: The Witches' Road
description: A seven-card journey spread for a long or uncertain undertaking, inspired by the 'Safe Passage' reading on the Witches' Road in the series Agatha All Along. You are the traveller; the cards map what you carry, what you lack, the road behind and ahead, the trials along the way, the unexpected boon, and where the road truly ends. Read it before a big change, a move, a new path of study or any quest of the heart.

positions.name: The Traveller
positions.meaning: Who you are as you set out on this road: your state, your strengths and the role you play in the journey.
positions.guide: Look at this card as a portrait of you setting out. What do you carry well, and what role are you playing on this journey?

positions.name: What's Missing
positions.meaning: What you lack or have not yet claimed; the gift, skill or companion the road will ask you to find.
positions.guide: Notice what seems absent in this card. What gift, skill or companion is the road going to ask you to find?

positions.name: The Path Behind
positions.meaning: The ground already travelled: past choices and experiences that brought you here and still walk with you.
positions.guide: Glance over your shoulder at the ground behind. Which past choice in this card still walks beside you?

positions.name: The Path Ahead
positions.meaning: The next stretch of road: the energy and events coming toward you.
positions.guide: Look down the road just ahead. What energy is coming toward you, and how can you meet it on your feet?

positions.name: The Obstacles
positions.meaning: The trial, test or danger on the road that must be faced rather than avoided.
positions.guide: Every road has its trial. What does this card ask you to face, and what would it cost to keep avoiding it?

positions.name: The Windfall
positions.meaning: The unexpected help, blessing or turn of fortune waiting along the way.
positions.guide: Keep your eyes open for a gift you did not plan for. Where might help or good fortune appear like the one in this card?

positions.name: The Destination
positions.meaning: Where this road truly leads, laid across the Traveller: the end of the journey and who you become by walking it.
positions.guide: Read this card across the Traveller. Where does this road truly end, and who do you become by walking all of it?

howToUse: Shuffle while picturing a winding road at dusk and asking for safe passage. Lay the Traveller in the centre, then lay the Destination sideways across its lower half, because who you are and where you are going are bound together. Around them, place five cards on the points of a pentagram: What's Missing at the top, the Path Behind at the bottom left, the Path Ahead at the far right, the Obstacles at the far left and the Windfall at the bottom right. Laid in that order, the five cards trace the star itself. Read the Traveller first, follow the star from point to point, and finish with the Destination.
intention: Down the Witches' Road I go; show me the way and what I need to know. Grant me safe passage, step by step, and show me true where the road leads.
bestTime: Any time you stand at the start of a journey; especially potent in autumn, from Mabon to Samhain, when the veil thins and the old roads open.

name: Daily Three: What to Know Today
description: A quick morning spread that tells you what you need to know for the day ahead: the energy surrounding you, the opportunity to embrace, and what to be mindful of. Draw it with your morning tea and keep it in your journal to see how each day unfolds.

positions.name: Today's Energy
positions.meaning: The main theme and atmosphere of your day: the energy you will be working with.
positions.guide: Sip your tea and take in this card's colours and mood. What kind of weather does it suggest for your day?

positions.name: Embrace Today
positions.meaning: The opportunity, gift or attitude to lean into today.
positions.guide: Find the gift in this card. What attitude or opportunity could you lean into, even in one small moment today?

positions.name: Be Mindful Today
positions.meaning: What to watch for, handle with care or avoid today, and the advice that keeps you on track.
positions.guide: Note this card in your journal as a gentle warning. Where might you need to slow down or take extra care today?

howToUse: Each morning, before checking your phone, take three slow breaths and shuffle while asking, 'What do I need to know today?' Lay three cards left to right. Read the first as the day's weather, the second as the door to walk through and the third as the stone in your shoe. Write one sentence for each card, then return in the evening to note what actually happened under Results in your Journal.
intention: Spirits of this new day, show me what I need to know: the energy around me, the gift to embrace, and the step to take with care.
bestTime: Every morning, all year round; especially helpful on Mondays (the Moon's day) and at the start of a new moon cycle.

name: The Moonlit Path: A Guided Celtic Cross
description: The classic ten-card Celtic Cross retold as a walk along a moonlit path, with a gentle guiding prompt at every step. It keeps the shape and depth of the traditional spread but names each position after the moon's light and shadow, so it is easier to remember and to feel. Perfect if the Celtic Cross has ever felt overwhelming: use the guided walk-through to reveal and reflect on one card at a time.

positions.name: The Moon Within
positions.meaning: The heart of the matter: where you stand right now and the energy at the centre of your question.
positions.guide: Breathe and look at this card first. What feeling rises before you even think about its meaning? That feeling is your starting point.

positions.name: The Crossing Shadow
positions.meaning: Laid across the first card: the obstacle, tension or shadow that crosses your path right now.
positions.guide: Every path by moonlight has shadows. Ask: is this shadow outside me, or one I am casting myself?

positions.name: Roots Beneath the Water
positions.meaning: The foundation below the surface: the deeper cause, buried feeling or old pattern feeding the situation.
positions.guide: Imagine your roots reaching into dark water. What is down there that you have not wanted to look at?

positions.name: The Waning Light
positions.meaning: The recent past that is now fading: what is leaving your life or loosening its hold.
positions.guide: As the moon wanes, it lets go. What is this card asking you to stop holding onto?

positions.name: The Silver Crown
positions.meaning: Above you, lit by the full moon: your highest aim, conscious hope or the best that can come of this.
positions.guide: Look up. If everything went as well as it could, what would this card look like in your life?

positions.name: The Waxing Light
positions.meaning: The near future growing toward you: the next phase that is gathering strength.
positions.guide: Like the crescent filling night by night, this is already on its way. How can you make room for it?

positions.name: The Seeker on the Path
positions.meaning: You as you walk this path: your attitude, your strengths and how you are meeting the situation.
positions.guide: Be honest and gentle with yourself. Do you recognise yourself in this card, or who you are becoming?

positions.name: The Night Around You
positions.meaning: Your surroundings: the people, places and influences around you, and how others see you.
positions.guide: Who walks beside you in the dark? Notice which helping or hindering hands this card points to.

positions.name: Whispers in the Dark
positions.meaning: Your hopes and fears, often tangled together: what you secretly long for and what you dread.
positions.guide: Hopes and fears often wear the same face. Which is this card for you tonight, or is it both?

positions.name: Where the Moonlit Path Leads
positions.meaning: The outcome if you keep walking as you are: where this path is heading.
positions.guide: This is a destination, not a doom. Read it alongside The Silver Crown: do they agree, and if not, what would you change?

howToUse: Read at night if you can, by candle or moonlight. Hold your question in mind and shuffle until the deck feels ready. Lay the first card at the centre and the second across it. Then place Roots Beneath the Water below, The Waning Light to the left, The Silver Crown above and The Waxing Light to the right, forming the cross. Finally, lay a staff of four cards up the right side, from The Seeker on the Path at the bottom to Where the Moonlit Path Leads at the top. After drawing, tap 'Walk the path, card by card' to turn over and reflect on one position at a time with its guiding prompt, then read the whole spread together.
intention: Moon above and path below, light my way and let me know: what is now, what lies beneath, and where this silver road will lead.
bestTime: Any night, but most powerful on the full moon, and in autumn and winter when the nights are long.

name: Daily Three: Morning, Afternoon, Evening
description: A simple timeline of your day: one card for each part of it, so you can see how the day is likely to flow and plan your energy.

positions.name: Morning
positions.meaning: How your day begins: the mood, energy or event that greets you in the first hours.
positions.guide: Picture yourself waking up inside this card. How does it set the tone for your first few hours?

positions.name: Afternoon
positions.meaning: The middle of your day: what you will be working with, meeting or dealing with as the day unfolds.
positions.guide: Midday is for getting things done. What task, person or challenge in this card might you meet after lunch?

positions.name: Evening
positions.meaning: How your day closes: what you carry home, how you wind down, and what the night brings.
positions.guide: Imagine the lamps coming on as you look. What will you carry home tonight, and how can you let the day go?

howToUse: Shuffle as you wake and ask, 'How will today unfold?' Lay three cards left to right like the sun crossing the sky. Read them as a little story; if one part looks heavy, plan extra kindness for yourself at that time of day. Check back at bedtime and note under Results which card proved truest.
intention: Show me the path of the sun today, from dawn to dusk, and light my way.
bestTime: Every day, all year round — morning is traditional, but any quiet moment works.

name: Daily Three: Focus, Challenge, Advice
description: A practical morning pull: what to concentrate on, what may trip you up, and the best way to handle the day.

positions.name: Today's Focus
positions.meaning: Where to put your attention and energy today.
positions.guide: Take a breath before the day rushes in. Where does this card ask you to put your attention and energy today?

positions.name: Today's Challenge
positions.meaning: The obstacle, mood or temptation most likely to trip you up today.
positions.guide: Forewarned is forearmed. What mood or temptation in this card might trip you up, and how will you spot it coming?

positions.name: Today's Advice
positions.meaning: How to meet the day well: the attitude or action that helps most.
positions.guide: Read this one as kindly advice from a friend. What attitude or small action will help you meet today well?

howToUse: Draw with your coffee or tea. Read the first card as your one priority, the second as the thing to watch for, and the third as your strategy. Write the advice card's key phrase somewhere you will see it during the day.
intention: Show me where to look, what to beware, and how to walk well today.
bestTime: Every day, all year round — morning is traditional, but any quiet moment works.

name: Daily Three: Head, Heart & Hands
description: Think, feel, do: a beloved three-card check-in that looks at your thoughts, your emotions and your actions for the day so all three can work together.

positions.name: Head
positions.meaning: Your thoughts today: what is on your mind and how to think about it clearly.
positions.guide: Tap your forehead lightly as you look. What thought keeps circling, and how might this card help you see it clearly?

positions.name: Heart
positions.meaning: Your feelings today: what your heart needs and is trying to tell you.
positions.guide: Rest a hand on your heart. What feeling in this card is asking to be heard today, even if it is quiet?

positions.name: Hands
positions.meaning: Your actions today: the practical step to take or the work to put your hands to.
positions.guide: Look at your own hands, then at the card. What practical thing will you put them to today?

howToUse: Shuffle while taking three breaths, one into your head, one into your heart and one into your hands. Lay the cards from left to right. Notice where they agree and where they pull in different directions; harmony between head, heart and hands is the day's quiet magic.
intention: Clear be my mind, open my heart, and steady my hands for what today asks.
bestTime: Every day, all year round — morning is traditional, but any quiet moment works.

name: Daily Three: Start, Stop, Continue
description: A coaching-style daily spread, popular for personal growth: something new to begin, something to let go of, and something that is already working.

positions.name: Start
positions.meaning: Something to begin, try or say yes to today.
positions.guide: Look for an open door in this card. What new thing could you try or say yes to before the day is out?

positions.name: Stop
positions.meaning: A habit, thought or behaviour to let go of today.
positions.guide: Notice what in this card feels heavy or familiar. Which habit or thought could you set down just for today?

positions.name: Continue
positions.meaning: What is already working; keep doing it and trust it.
positions.guide: Something is already working. What does this card affirm that you should keep doing, and can you trust it?

howToUse: Ask, 'What does today need from me?' Lay three cards in a row. Take the Start card as a tiny experiment for the day, the Stop card as one thing to notice and release, and the Continue card as encouragement. Track them for a week in your Journal to see your growth.
intention: Show me what to begin, what to release, and what to keep tending.
bestTime: Every day, all year round — morning is traditional, but any quiet moment works.

name: Daily Three: Gratitude, Growth & Guidance
description: A gentle, uplifting daily spread for mindful mornings or evenings: something to be grateful for, an area to grow in, and a word of guidance from spirit.

positions.name: Gratitude
positions.meaning: A blessing in your life right now to notice and give thanks for.
positions.guide: Take a soft breath and smile at this card. What small blessing in your life today does it remind you to thank?

positions.name: Growth
positions.meaning: Where you are being invited to stretch, learn or heal today.
positions.guide: Ask where you are being stretched today. Is this card inviting you to learn something, try something or heal something?

positions.name: Guidance
positions.meaning: A message from your guides, ancestors or higher self for today.
positions.guide: Imagine your guides or ancestors placing this card in your hands. What single sentence of advice would they give you for today?

howToUse: Light a candle if you like. Hold the deck to your heart and ask to be shown the day's blessings and lessons. Read the Gratitude card first and say thank you aloud; let the Growth card be a gentle intention; keep the Guidance card on your altar or as your phone wallpaper for the day.
intention: With a thankful heart I ask: show me my blessings, my growing edge, and the word I need today.
bestTime: Every day, all year round — morning is traditional, but any quiet moment works.

name: Jack-o'-Lantern: The Carved Face
description: A nine-card Halloween spread laid out as a glowing jack-o'-lantern, from its curling stem to its wide carved grin. Old lore says the lantern's face frightens off wandering spirits while its candle guides friendly ones home. Read it on Halloween night to see what you are guarding against, what you are lighting the way for, and what joy is grinning back at you.

positions.name: The Curling Stem
positions.meaning: What roots this season of your life and keeps you connected to the vine you grew from.
positions.guide: Picture the stem still attached to the vine. What in this card keeps you nourished and connected as the year darkens?

positions.name: The Watchful Left Eye
positions.meaning: What you are keeping an eye on in your own life: the inner matter that needs your attention.
positions.guide: Look through this carved eye inward. What part of your own life is this card asking you to watch more closely this autumn?

positions.name: The Watchful Right Eye
positions.meaning: What you are keeping an eye on in the world around you: people, signs and outside forces.
positions.guide: Look through this eye outward. Which person, sign or situation around you does this card say deserves a careful watch?

positions.name: The Candle Within
positions.meaning: The steady flame burning inside you that keeps the whole lantern glowing.
positions.guide: Imagine a candle flickering behind this card. What inner light keeps you shining, and how can you protect that flame tonight?

positions.name: The Grin's Left Corner
positions.meaning: A small fear or worry you can laugh at now that you see it in the lantern light.
positions.guide: Every grin starts at one corner. What worry in this card looks smaller and sillier once you shine a light on it?

positions.name: The First Carved Tooth
positions.meaning: What you have cut away this year to make room for light.
positions.guide: Think of the pumpkin flesh you scooped out. What did you remove this year, and how has it let more light through?

positions.name: The Middle Tooth
positions.meaning: The protection this lantern offers: what wards off unwelcome energy from your doorstep.
positions.guide: This is the lantern's fiercest tooth. What does this card guard against, and how can you set it on your doorstep tonight?

positions.name: The Last Carved Tooth
positions.meaning: The friendly spirit, ancestor or helper your light is calling home.
positions.guide: Lanterns guide kindly spirits home. Who or what is this card welcoming back to your hearth this Halloween?

positions.name: The Grin's Right Corner
positions.meaning: The delight, mischief or celebration waiting for you as the season turns.
positions.guide: Let the grin finish its curl. What fun or playful joy does this card promise once the spooky night is through?

howToUse: Light a candle, or a real jack-o'-lantern if you have one, and shuffle while tracing a smiling face on the deck with your finger. Lay the Curling Stem at the top centre, then the two eyes side by side below it, and the Candle Within in the middle as the nose. Lay the grin along the bottom from left to right: the left corner raised slightly, the three carved teeth in a row, and the right corner raised to match. Read from the stem down through the eyes and candle, then follow the grin from corner to corner, letting the faint gold line trace the smile.
intention: Carved face and candle bright, guard my door this Halloween night. Light the way for friends to come, and show me what I'm grinning from.
bestTime: Halloween night (Oct 31), or any evening in late October once the pumpkins are carved.

name: Trick or Treat: The Doorstep
description: A simple three-card Halloween spread for knocking on the door of the coming season. Behind the costume, ask what is tricking you and what sweet treat is waiting to be shared. Perfect for a quick reading between visitors on Halloween night or for beginners just learning to read.

positions.name: The Costume You Wear
positions.meaning: The role or disguise you are wearing right now, and what it lets you be.
positions.guide: Look at this card as tonight's costume. Who are you pretending to be lately, and what does the disguise let you get away with?

positions.name: The Trick at the Door
positions.meaning: What is fooling you, testing you or playing a prank on your expectations.
positions.guide: Every doorstep has a trickster. What in this card might be fooling you, and how can you laugh and see through it?

positions.name: The Treat in the Bowl
positions.meaning: The sweet reward, kindness or good surprise coming your way.
positions.guide: Reach into the bowl and take what is offered. What sweet thing does this card promise, and who could you share it with?

howToUse: Shuffle while knocking three times on the deck and saying 'trick or treat'. Lay the Costume You Wear at the top centre, then the Trick at the Door below it on the left and the Treat in the Bowl below it on the right, like a little doorstep with two paths. Read the Costume first, then the Trick, and finish with the Treat so the reading ends on something sweet.
intention: Knock, knock, at the door; show me what the night's in store. Help me see the trick that's true, and share the treat that's coming through.
bestTime: Halloween night (Oct 31), or any evening in the last week of October.

name: The Haunted House and the Black Cat
description: A seven-card Halloween spread shaped like a creaky old house with a black cat waiting on the step. Wander from the dusty attic to the cellar stair to meet the ghosts of your own story and learn which ones are ready to be laid to rest. Read it on Halloween when you feel haunted by old habits, memories or worries and want a familiar to guide you through.

positions.name: The Dusty Attic
positions.meaning: Something forgotten and stored away that still holds meaning or power.
positions.guide: Climb the attic stairs and lift the sheet off this card. What did you pack away long ago that wants to be remembered now?

positions.name: The Lit Window
positions.meaning: What you show to passers-by: the face of your life you let others see.
positions.guide: Imagine neighbours glancing up at this glowing window. What do they see of you, and is it the whole truth?

positions.name: The Shuttered Window
positions.meaning: What you keep hidden behind closed shutters, even from yourself.
positions.guide: Ease open the shutter on this card. What have you been keeping out of sight, and would a little light really hurt?

positions.name: The Parlour Ghost
positions.meaning: An old memory, habit or relationship that still lingers in your everyday rooms.
positions.guide: Sit with this gentle ghost in the parlour. What lingering memory or habit does it show, and is it ready to rest?

positions.name: The Creaking Door
positions.meaning: The threshold you are being invited to cross, despite the creak and the nerves.
positions.guide: Hear the hinge groan as this door opens. What threshold is in front of you, and what would help you step through?

positions.name: The Cellar Stair
positions.meaning: The deeper fear or shadow beneath the house that steadies you once faced.
positions.guide: Take one step down the cellar stair with this card. What fear lives below, and what strength might you find there?

positions.name: The Black Cat on the Step
positions.meaning: Your familiar's message: the wise, lucky guidance that sees you safely through the haunting.
positions.guide: The black cat waits for you outside. What advice does this card purr to you about leaving the haunted house wiser?

howToUse: Shuffle by candlelight and knock gently on the deck as if at an old front door. Lay the Dusty Attic at the very top as the roof peak, then the Lit Window below it on the left and the Shuttered Window below it on the right. Lay the ground floor in a row beneath them: the Parlour Ghost on the left, the Creaking Door in the centre and the Cellar Stair on the right. Finally, set the Black Cat on the Step below the Creaking Door. Read from the attic down through the house, room by room, and let the cat have the last word.
intention: Creaking stair and candle's glow, show me the ghosts I need to know. Black cat, guide me through the door, and let me be haunted nevermore.
bestTime: Halloween night (Oct 31), or any dark evening in October when old memories come knocking.

name: Christmas Tree: Star on Top
description: A nine-card Christmas and Yuletide spread laid out as an evergreen tree, from its sturdy trunk to the shining star on top, with two gifts tucked underneath. The evergreen has been brought indoors in midwinter for centuries as a promise that life endures. Read it while you decorate or on Christmas Eve to celebrate what has grown in you this year and what you hope to crown it with.

positions.name: The Evergreen Trunk
positions.meaning: What has kept you standing through the whole year: your steady core.
positions.guide: Rest your hand on the trunk. What in this card held you upright through this year's storms, and how can you honour it?

positions.name: The Low Bough of Memory
positions.meaning: A treasured memory from the year that deserves a place on the tree.
positions.guide: Hang this card like an old ornament. Which moment from this year do you most want to keep and remember?

positions.name: The Tinsel Bough
positions.meaning: What made this year sparkle: the joys, lights and little celebrations.
positions.guide: Let the tinsel catch the light. What made your year glitter, even briefly, and how can you invite more of it?

positions.name: The Low Bough of Lessons
positions.meaning: A hard-won lesson from the year that now makes you stronger.
positions.guide: Some ornaments are heavy. What lesson does this card hang here, and how has carrying it made your branches stronger?

positions.name: The Garland of Kin
positions.meaning: The people and loved ones woven around you this season.
positions.guide: Follow the garland from branch to branch. Who does this card wrap you up with, and how can you show them warmth?

positions.name: The Bough of Wishes
positions.meaning: The heartfelt wish you hang on the tree for the year to come.
positions.guide: Tie your wish onto this bough like a ribbon. What does this card hint you truly want the new year to bring?

positions.name: The Star at the Top
positions.meaning: The guiding light that crowns your year and points the way forward.
positions.guide: Look up to the very top. What bright hope or guidance does this star offer to lead you into the new year?

positions.name: The Gift You Give
positions.meaning: The gift of yourself that you are ready to offer others this season.
positions.guide: Wrap this card in your mind. What gift of time, talent or kindness are you ready to give, and to whom?

positions.name: The Gift You Receive
