positions.meaning: The blessing waiting under the tree for you, if you are willing to unwrap it.
positions.guide: Untie the ribbon slowly. What blessing does this card hold for you, and are you ready to accept it gratefully?

howToUse: Shuffle with a sprig of evergreen, a pine cone or a string of lights nearby, breathing in the scent of the season. Lay the Evergreen Trunk at the bottom centre, then the three lower boughs in a row above it from left to right, then the two upper boughs above those. Crown the tree with the Star at the Top, and tuck the Gift You Give to the left of the trunk and the Gift You Receive to its right. Read from the trunk upward to the star, then open the two gifts last.
intention: Evergreen and shining star, show me who and where we are. Bless the gifts I give and take, and light the year for all our sake.
bestTime: While trimming the tree, on Christmas Eve (Dec 24) or any evening between the Winter Solstice and New Year.

name: The Hearthside Stocking
description: A gentle four-card Christmas and Yuletide spread laid out in the shape of a stocking hung by the fire. Whether Saint Nicholas, the Yule spirits or simple family love fills it, a stocking is a promise that someone remembers you. Read it on Christmas Eve or any winter night to see what you are ready to receive and what little surprise is tucked in the toe.

positions.name: The Woollen Cuff
positions.meaning: What you are hanging up hopefully: the openness you bring to the season.
positions.guide: Hang your stocking by the fire. What does this card say you are hoping for, and how open are you to receiving it?

positions.name: The Long Wool Leg
positions.meaning: What already fills your life and keeps you warm, though you may overlook it.
positions.guide: Reach down the stocking. What good thing in this card is already filling your life that you might be taking for granted?

positions.name: The Heel's Turn
positions.meaning: The bend in the road this year: the change you have walked through.
positions.guide: Feel the heel curve. What turning point from this year does this card show, and what did it teach your feet?

positions.name: The Treat in the Toe
positions.meaning: The small, sweet surprise waiting at the very end of the season.
positions.guide: Wiggle your fingers all the way into the toe. What small, delightful surprise does this card tuck in for you?

howToUse: Warm your hands by a fire, candle or mug of something hot, and shuffle while thinking of someone who once filled a stocking for you. Lay the Woollen Cuff at the top, then the Long Wool Leg directly below it and the Heel's Turn below that. Lay the Treat in the Toe to the right of the Heel's Turn so the four cards form a stocking. Read from the cuff down to the toe, saving the surprise for last.
intention: By the hearth my stocking hung, warm with songs the old year sung. Fill me up with what is true, and tuck a little joy in too.
bestTime: Christmas Eve (Dec 24), Saint Nicholas' Eve (Dec 5), or any cosy winter evening by the fire.

name: Star of Wonder: The Guiding Light
description: A six-card Christmas and Yuletide spread laid out as a five-pointed star with your sense of wonder at its heart. In the old carols, travellers followed a bright star through the longest nights carrying gifts to an unknown destination. Read it in the deep of winter, from the Solstice to Twelfth Night, when you need to rediscover wonder and find the light worth following.

positions.name: The Wonder Within
positions.meaning: The childlike sense of awe that still lives in you, waiting to be rekindled.
positions.guide: Gaze at this card as you once gazed at winter lights. Where does wonder still live in you, and how can you rekindle it?

positions.name: The Star Rising
positions.meaning: The light calling you forward this season: the hope or vision worth following.
positions.guide: Look up at the rising star in this card. What hope or vision is calling you, and are you willing to follow it?

positions.name: The Long Winter Night
positions.meaning: The darkness you are travelling through and what it is teaching you.
positions.guide: Walk through the long night of this card. What darkness are you crossing, and what is it quietly teaching you?

positions.name: The Gift You Carry
positions.meaning: The treasure, talent or offering you bring with you on the journey.
positions.guide: Open your travelling bag. What treasure in this card are you carrying, and who is it really meant for?

positions.name: The Fellow Travellers
positions.meaning: The companions, guides or kindred spirits walking beside you.
positions.guide: Glance at who rides beside you. Which companion or guide does this card show, and how might you thank them?

positions.name: The Arrival at Dawn
positions.meaning: Where the star is leading you and the blessing waiting at the journey's end.
positions.guide: Imagine the sky turning gold as you arrive. What blessing waits where this star leads, and how will you greet it?

howToUse: Turn down the lights and shuffle by a single candle or a string of fairy lights, picturing one bright star over a snowy road. Lay the Wonder Within in the centre, then the Star Rising at the top point, the Long Winter Night at the bottom left point, the Gift You Carry at the far right point, the Fellow Travellers at the far left point and the Arrival at Dawn at the bottom right point. Laid in that order, the five outer cards trace the star in one stroke, shown by the faint gold line. Read the centre first, then follow the star from point to point.
intention: Star of wonder, shining bright, guide me through the longest night. Show me the gift I carry true, and the dawn I'm walking to.
bestTime: Any night from the Winter Solstice (around Dec 21) to Twelfth Night (Jan 5), especially on a clear, starry night.

name: New Year's Eve: The Midnight Clock
description: A ring of cards laid like a clock face for New Year's Eve, with the heart of the coming year at its centre. As the old year ticks down to midnight, each hour on the dial shows a different part of the twelve months ahead: where things begin, what powers you, what tests you and where joy is waiting. Read it in the last hours of December 31st to greet the new year with clear eyes.

positions.name: The First Chime
positions.meaning: What truly begins for you as the new year strikes.
positions.guide: Listen for the first chime of the year. What fresh start does this card ring in, and what is the very first step you could take toward it in January?

positions.name: The Winding Key
positions.meaning: The source of energy and motivation that will keep you going all year.
positions.guide: Every clock needs winding. What in this card keeps your spring tight and your hands moving? Name one way to wind yourself up when you run slow.

positions.name: The Swinging Pendulum
positions.meaning: Where balance will be needed between two pulls in the year ahead.
positions.guide: Watch the pendulum swing between two sides. What two pulls does this card show you, and where is the steady middle you can return to?

positions.name: The Slow Hour
positions.meaning: The area of life where patience is asked and progress comes gradually.
positions.guide: Some hours drag. Where does this card ask you to wait without giving up? Promise yourself one small, patient habit for this part of the year.

positions.name: The Half-Past Lesson
positions.meaning: The challenge at the year's midpoint and the lesson hidden inside it.
positions.guide: Imagine the clock at half past, the year half spent. What test does this card bring, and what wiser person will you be on the other side of it?

positions.name: The Ticking Doubt
positions.meaning: The worry or fear that may tick away in the background of your year.
positions.guide: Hear the quiet ticking you try to ignore. What doubt lives in this card? Say it out loud, then decide whether it deserves your time.

positions.name: The Gilded Hour
positions.meaning: A golden stretch of joy, luck or celebration coming in the new year.
positions.guide: Every year holds a golden hour. What happiness does this card promise? Picture the moment clearly and raise an imaginary glass to it now.

positions.name: The Last Chime of the Year
positions.meaning: Where the year is heading as it comes full circle to next December.
positions.guide: Let the hands sweep all the way round. Looking at this card, who do you hope to be when the clock strikes twelve again next December?

positions.name: The Stroke of Twelve
positions.meaning: The central theme and spirit of the whole new year.
positions.guide: This card sits where the clock's hands meet. What single word or image sums up the year ahead? Write it down and keep it somewhere you will see it.

howToUse: Shuffle as the evening deepens on New Year's Eve, counting down from twelve under your breath. Lay the First Chime at the top of the clock, then continue clockwise round the dial: the Winding Key at half past one, the Swinging Pendulum at three, the Slow Hour at half past four, the Half-Past Lesson at six, the Ticking Doubt at half past seven, the Gilded Hour at nine and the Last Chime of the Year at half past ten. Place the Stroke of Twelve in the very centre where the hands meet. Read clockwise round the ring from the top, then finish with the centre card as the theme that ties the year together.
intention: As the old year ends and the new bells chime, I open my eyes to the turning of time. Show me the hours that are coming my way, and bless every one from night into day.
bestTime: New Year's Eve (Dec 31), ideally in the hour before midnight, or any time in the first week of January.

name: New Year's Day: The Champagne Toast
description: A simple five-card spread laid in the shape of a raised champagne glass, perfect for New Year's Day resolutions. From the foot to the rim, the cards show what holds you up, what fills your glass and the bubbling intention rising to the top, ending with the clink of glasses from those who cheer you on. Pour yourself something sparkling and toast the year you are choosing.

positions.name: The Foot of the Glass
positions.meaning: The strength or lesson from last year that gives you a steady base.
positions.guide: A glass needs a firm foot. What did last year give you that you can stand on now? Thank it out loud before you look up the stem.

positions.name: The Slender Stem
positions.meaning: The habit or quality that will keep your resolution upright.
positions.guide: Hold the glass by its stem so the bubbles stay bright. What steady habit in this card will help you keep your resolution through February and beyond?

positions.name: The Golden Pour
positions.meaning: What will fill your year with richness, pleasure and plenty.
positions.guide: Watch the glass fill with gold. What abundance is pouring in from this card? Notice where in your life there is room to receive it.

positions.name: The Rising Bubble
positions.meaning: The resolution or intention that wants to rise to the top this year.
positions.guide: Bubbles rise all on their own. What intention keeps floating up in this card? Turn it into one clear sentence beginning with "This year I will".

positions.name: The Clink of Glasses
positions.meaning: The people, allies or support who will celebrate your success with you.
positions.guide: A toast is better shared. Who does this card bring to mind as someone who will cheer you on? Consider telling them your resolution today.

howToUse: Shuffle while holding a glass of something sparkling, whether champagne, cider or fizzy water, and think about the year you want. Build the glass from the bottom up: lay the Foot of the Glass at the base, the Slender Stem just above it and the Golden Pour above that as the bowl. Place the Rising Bubble and the Clink of Glasses side by side across the top as the rim, the Rising Bubble on the left. Read from the foot upward, finishing at the rim, then take a sip and speak your resolution as a toast.
intention: I raise my glass to the year that is new; let every bright bubble of hope come true. Steady my hand and fill up my cup, and lift me as surely as bubbles rise up.
bestTime: New Year's Day (Jan 1), or whenever you sit down to write your resolutions in early January.

name: New Year: The Year's Doorway
description: A seven-card spread shaped like an open doorway between the old year and the new, inspired by the old custom of opening the door at midnight to let the old year out and the new year in. The left side of the frame holds what you are leaving behind, the right side what comes in to greet you, and the key in the middle shows how to cross well. Use it between Christmas and the first days of January to close one chapter with grace.

positions.name: The Last Ember of the Old Year
positions.meaning: What is still burning from the old year and is ready to be honoured and let go.
positions.guide: See the last ember glowing on the old hearth. What in this card are you ready to thank and let burn out? Blow gently, as if cooling it.

positions.name: What Stays Behind the Door
positions.meaning: The burden, habit or story you will not carry into the new year.
positions.guide: Some things are left in the old room. What weight in this card will you set down here? Picture closing the door softly on it.

positions.name: The Blessing Over the Lintel
positions.meaning: The protection and blessing that watches over your crossing.
positions.guide: Imagine a sprig of greenery hung above the door. What blessing does this card place over your head as you step through? Accept it with thanks.

positions.name: The Key in Your Hand
positions.meaning: The attitude or action that unlocks the new year for you.
positions.guide: Feel the cool weight of a key in your palm. What quality in this card opens the way forward? Name one place you can use it this week.

positions.name: The Threshold Stone
positions.meaning: The step you must take, however small, to leave the old year truly behind.
positions.guide: The threshold is a single step, but you must take it. What does this card ask you to do to cross? Decide when you will do it.

positions.name: The First Footer
positions.meaning: The first new energy, person or opportunity to enter your year.
positions.guide: Old custom says the first guest over the threshold brings the year's luck. Who or what does this card show arriving first? How will you welcome them?

positions.name: The Warm Room Within
positions.meaning: The comfort, growth and belonging waiting on the new side of the door.
positions.guide: Step into the warm, lamplit room of the new year. What comfort or growth is waiting for you in this card? Let yourself feel at home there.

howToUse: Before you begin, open a door or window for a moment to let fresh winter air move through the room, then shuffle. Lay the Blessing Over the Lintel at the top, then build the left side of the frame with the Last Ember of the Old Year above What Stays Behind the Door, and the right side with the First Footer above the Warm Room Within. Place the Key in Your Hand in the open doorway between them and the Threshold Stone at the bottom. Read the left side first, then the lintel, the key and the threshold, and finish on the right side as you step into the new year. Close the door afterwards as a sign the crossing is done.
intention: Old year, go gently out the door; I will not carry you anymore. New year, step in and bring your light; I cross the threshold, blessed tonight.
bestTime: The quiet days between Christmas and New Year's, on New Year's Eve at midnight, or any time in the first week of January.

name: Valentine's Day: The Valentine's Heart
description: A nine-card spread laid in the shape of a Valentine's heart, tracing how love flows through your whole life and not just one romance. The outline follows love from what you give and receive, through old hurts and sweet surprises, down to the point where it is headed, with the beating heart of it all at the centre. Read it on Valentine's Day whether you are partnered, single or somewhere in between.

positions.name: The Lace Edge
positions.meaning: How love is offered to you, and how open you are to receiving it.
positions.guide: Like the lace trim on an old valentine, this card shows love reaching toward you. Where are you letting it in, and where are you brushing it off?

positions.name: The Paper Heart
positions.meaning: How you give love and express affection to others.
positions.guide: Think of a heart you once cut out of paper for someone. How does this card describe the way you give love? Is it reaching the right people?

positions.name: The Cleft of the Heart
positions.meaning: The tender dip where love and longing meet: what you most desire in love right now.
positions.guide: Every heart has a soft dip at the top. What longing rests in this card? Let yourself admit it without judging it.

positions.name: The Old Love Letter
positions.meaning: A past love or relationship whose influence you still carry.
positions.guide: Unfold an old letter in your mind. What past love does this card bring back, and what did it teach you about what you want now?

positions.name: The Sweet Surprise
positions.meaning: An unexpected joy or tenderness coming your way in love.
positions.guide: Like a box of sweets left on the doorstep, this card brings a surprise. What unexpected affection could arrive soon? Stay curious enough to notice it.

positions.name: The Thorn on the Rose
positions.meaning: The fear, wound or pattern that pricks you when you try to love.
positions.guide: Roses come with thorns. What hurt or habit in this card makes you pull your hand back? Breathe into it gently and ask what it needs.

positions.name: The Ribbon and Bow
positions.meaning: What ties love together for you: commitment, trust or shared joy.
positions.guide: A bow holds the gift together. What does this card say keeps love tied securely in your life? How can you tie that bow a little tighter?

positions.name: The Beating Heart
positions.meaning: The truth at the centre of your love life right now.
positions.guide: Place a hand over your own heart as you look at this card. What is the honest heartbeat of your love life today?

positions.name: The Point of the Heart
positions.meaning: Where your love life is heading in the season ahead.
positions.guide: All lines of a heart meet at its point. Where is this card leading your love? What one small act this week moves you toward it?

howToUse: Light a red or pink candle and shuffle while thinking of every kind of love in your life: romantic, family, friendship and the love you hold for yourself. Lay the Lace Edge and the Paper Heart as the two rounded tops of the heart, with the Cleft of the Heart in the dip between them. Place the Old Love Letter at the far left and the Sweet Surprise at the far right, then the Thorn on the Rose and the Ribbon and Bow lower down as the heart narrows, and the Point of the Heart at the very bottom. The Beating Heart sits in the centre. Read the two tops and the cleft first, then follow the sides down to the point, and finish with the Beating Heart.
intention: Heart of my heart, open and true, show me the love that is flowing through. All that I give and all I receive, let me see clearly and let me believe.
bestTime: Valentine's Day (Feb 14), or any Friday evening in February, Friday being the day of Venus.

name: Valentine's Day: Cupid's Arrow
description: A six-card spread laid as Cupid's arrow in flight, striking a heart at its tip. Use it on Valentine's Day to ask where love's arrow is aimed: what feathers its flight, what carries it forward and what happens when it lands. It suits anyone wondering about an attraction, a crush or the spark they hope is coming.

positions.name: The Upper Fletching
positions.meaning: The hope or wish that sends love on its way.
positions.guide: Feathers guide an arrow straight. What hope in this card steers your heart? Say the wish quietly to yourself, as if whispering it to Cupid.

positions.name: The Lower Fletching
positions.meaning: The hidden fear or hesitation that could send the arrow off course.
positions.guide: One crooked feather can bend the flight. What hesitation does this card reveal? Ask whether it is protecting you or simply holding you back.

positions.name: The Drawn Bowstring
positions.meaning: The courage and energy you put behind your feelings.
positions.guide: Feel the tension of a bowstring pulled back. How much courage does this card show you putting behind your feelings? Is it time to let go and loose the arrow?

positions.name: The Arrow in Flight
positions.meaning: How the attraction or connection is unfolding right now.
positions.guide: The arrow is in the air. What does this card say about how the spark is moving between you and another? Notice its speed and direction.

positions.name: The Struck Heart
positions.meaning: The heart the arrow is aimed at: the person or love you are drawn to.
positions.guide: Look at the heart waiting at the arrow's tip. What does this card tell you about the one you are drawn to, and how open is their heart?

positions.name: The Arrowhead's Mark
positions.meaning: Laid across the Struck Heart: what happens when love finds its mark.
positions.guide: See the arrow land across the heart. What does this card say will come of the connection? Ask yourself if this is the outcome you truly want.

howToUse: Shuffle with a red ribbon or a single rose beside you, picturing the person or kind of love you are wondering about. Lay the Upper Fletching at the top left and the Lower Fletching at the bottom left as the arrow's feathers. Lay the Drawn Bowstring and the Arrow in Flight in a row between them, running to the right, then the Struck Heart at the far right. Lay the Arrowhead's Mark sideways across the lower half of the Struck Heart, as if the arrow has pierced it. Read from the feathers along the shaft to the heart, and finish with the Arrowhead's Mark.
intention: Feathered and true, let Cupid's arrow fly; show me where it lands and show me why. Guide my heart with courage, aim it clear and kind, and let me know the love I am meant to find.
bestTime: Valentine's Day (Feb 14), or the days just before it when a spark is on your mind.

name: Valentine's Day: A Valentine to Myself
description: A gentle five-card spread laid like a sealed valentine envelope, written from you to you. Made for single folks, or anyone who wants to spend Valentine's Day courting their own heart, it reveals the sweet words you deserve to hear, the gift you can give yourself and the promise sealed at the centre. A cosy, celebratory reading to pair with a treat and a candle.

positions.name: Dear Me
positions.meaning: How you are greeting yourself this Valentine's Day: the tone of your inner voice.
positions.guide: Every valentine begins with a greeting. How does this card say you speak to yourself lately? Try greeting yourself warmly, out loud, by name.

positions.name: The Sweet Nothing
positions.meaning: The loving words or compliment you most need to hear from yourself.
positions.guide: What tender words does this card whisper to you? Write them on a small heart of paper and tuck it somewhere you will find later.

positions.name: The Box of Chocolates
positions.meaning: The treat, pleasure or act of care you can gift yourself today.
positions.guide: Lift the lid and look inside. What delight does this card suggest you give yourself today? Choose one and actually do it before bed.

positions.name: With Love, From Me
positions.meaning: The quality you love in yourself and how to let it shine more.
positions.guide: Sign the valentine with your own name. What quality in this card are you proud of? How could you let it be seen this year?

positions.name: The Wax Seal
positions.meaning: The promise of self-love you seal into your heart this year.
positions.guide: Press the seal into warm wax. What promise to yourself does this card ask you to keep? Make it simple enough to hold to.

howToUse: Run a bath, make a cup of something sweet or light a pink candle, then shuffle while telling yourself one thing you love about who you are. Lay the cards in a diamond like a valentine envelope: Dear Me at the top, the Sweet Nothing on the left, the Box of Chocolates on the right and With Love, From Me at the bottom. Place the Wax Seal in the centre to close the envelope. Read the four points from the top, round the left, right and bottom, then read the Wax Seal last as your promise.
intention: This valentine is written to me, sealed with the love I am learning to see. I am worthy, I am whole, I am dear; I choose myself this day and all year.
bestTime: Valentine's Day (Feb 14), especially if you are spending it solo, or any evening you need a little self-romance.

name: St. Patrick's Shamrock
description: A gentle St. Patrick's Day spread laid in the shape of a shamrock: three leaves for heart, home and hope, a stem that roots you, and a lucky fourth leaf tucked into the centre. Read it on March 17th to take stock of the green, growing things in your life and to invite a little luck in as spring arrives.

positions.name: The Leaf of the Heart
positions.meaning: The love, warmth and connection quietly growing in your life right now.
positions.guide: Look for the warmth in this card. Who or what is your heart reaching toward this spring?

positions.name: The Leaf of the Hearth
positions.meaning: Your home, family and the daily ground you stand on.
positions.guide: Picture this card sitting at your own kitchen table. What does your home need from you this season?

positions.name: The Leaf of Hope
positions.meaning: The wish or dream that is unfurling toward the light.
positions.guide: Name one hope out loud while you study this card. What first green shoot of it can you already see?

positions.name: The Shamrock Stem
positions.meaning: What roots and steadies you, the strength that feeds all three leaves.
positions.guide: Trace this card like a stem going down into soil. What steady habit or belief keeps all three leaves fed?

positions.name: The Lucky Fourth Leaf
positions.meaning: The rare stroke of luck or blessing that is ready to find you.
positions.guide: This is your four-leaf find. What small, rare blessing is hiding in plain sight, and how can you say yes to it?

howToUse: Shuffle with a sprig of clover, a green candle or a pinch of salt nearby, thinking of what you would like to grow. Lay the Leaf of the Heart at the top, the Leaf of the Hearth to the lower left and the Leaf of Hope to the lower right, then set the Shamrock Stem below them. Last, tuck the Lucky Fourth Leaf into the centre where the three leaves meet. Read the three leaves first, then the stem, and save the lucky card for last.
intention: Three leaves for heart, hearth and hope, and one more for luck; let what is green in me grow.
bestTime: St. Patrick's Day (March 17), or any morning in mid-March when the first green shoots appear.

name: Pot of Gold at the End of the Rainbow
description: A St. Patrick's Day spread that follows a rainbow from the first raindrop, up and over its arc, and down to the pot of gold waiting at its end. Use it to trace a goal from where it begins to the reward it promises, and to spot the colours of help along the way. A cheerful reading for March 17th, or for any time a rainbow catches your eye.

positions.name: The First Raindrop
positions.meaning: The small trouble, longing or storm that set this goal in motion.
positions.guide: Every rainbow needs rain first. What storm or longing in this card started you on this path?

positions.name: The Red Band
positions.meaning: The passion and courage that lift you off the ground.
positions.guide: Feel the fire in this card. Where does your courage come from, and how can you stoke it today?

positions.name: The Golden Band
positions.meaning: The confidence and joy that carry your effort higher.
positions.guide: Let this card warm you like sunlight. What brings you joy in the work itself, not only the reward?

positions.name: The Green Band
positions.meaning: The peak of the arc: growth, health and the steady work at the top of the climb.
positions.guide: This is the highest point of your rainbow. What steady, green work is needed right now to keep it shining?

positions.name: The Blue Band
positions.meaning: The calm truth or honest word that guides your descent toward the goal.
positions.guide: Read this card as cool, clear water. What honest truth do you need to speak or hear as you come down the arc?

positions.name: The Violet Band
positions.meaning: The intuition, magic and quiet faith that bring you the last stretch.
positions.guide: Close your eyes for a breath before reading this card. What is your intuition whispering about the final stretch?

positions.name: The Pot of Gold
positions.meaning: The reward that waits at the end of the rainbow and what it is truly worth.
positions.guide: Lift the lid on this card. What treasure is really waiting for you, and is it the gold you expected?

howToUse: Shuffle while holding a coin, ideally a gold-coloured one, and picture a rainbow after rain. Lay the First Raindrop at the bottom left, then build the arc from left to right: the Red Band above it, the Golden Band, the Green Band at the very top, the Blue Band and the Violet Band coming down the right side. Set the Pot of Gold at the bottom right, under the end of the rainbow. Read from the raindrop, over the arc, and finish with the gold.
intention: From the first drop of rain to the gold at the rainbow's end, I follow every colour and welcome the treasure meant for me.
bestTime: St. Patrick's Day (March 17), or right after a spring rain shower; lovely in any week of March.

name: Luck of the Irish: Celtic Knot
description: An eight-card St. Patrick's Day spread woven like a Celtic trinity knot, where three loops of luck, love and wisdom pass through one heart and never break. It shows how the threads of your life bind together, where luck is tangled and where it flows freely. Best for deep reflection on March 17th, or whenever you want to understand how the pieces of your fortune connect.

positions.name: The Heart of the Knot
positions.meaning: Your core self, the centre through which every thread of your luck passes.
positions.guide: Sit with this card as the heart of your weave. What part of you do all your threads keep returning to?

positions.name: The Tangle
positions.meaning: The snag or crossed thread that is knotting up your luck right now.
positions.guide: Read this card laid across your heart. Which thread is pulling tight, and what would loosen it gently?

positions.name: The Loop of Fortune
positions.meaning: The point of the knot where luck, chance and opportunity gather.
positions.guide: Look at this card as your lucky loop. Where is chance gathering for you, and are you watching for it?

positions.name: The Thread to Fortune
positions.meaning: The connection carrying luck toward love and loyalty.
positions.guide: Follow this thread with your finger. How does your good fortune flow toward the people you care about?

positions.name: The Loop of Kinship
positions.meaning: The love, friendship and kin who are woven into your luck.
positions.guide: See the faces in this card. Whose love is woven into your luck, and how can you honour them this week?

positions.name: The Thread Beneath
positions.meaning: The hidden connection between love and wisdom, often an inheritance or old story.
positions.guide: This thread runs under everything. What old family story or inherited gift does this card bring up?

positions.name: The Loop of Wisdom
positions.meaning: The knowledge and hard-won sense that guide how you use your luck.
positions.guide: Let this card speak like an old storyteller. What lesson would help you spend your luck wisely?

positions.name: The Thread Returning
positions.meaning: How wisdom loops back into fortune, closing the knot and beginning it again.
positions.guide: Every knot returns to its start. What have you learned that will bring fresh luck around again?

howToUse: Shuffle slowly while tracing a knot shape on the deck with your finger, or while winding a green thread around your hand. Place the Heart of the Knot in the centre and lay the Tangle sideways across its lower half. Set the Loop of Fortune at the top, the Loop of Kinship at the bottom right and the Loop of Wisdom at the bottom left, then lay the three threads between them: the Thread to Fortune on the right, the Thread Beneath at the bottom centre and the Thread Returning on the left. Read the heart and tangle first, then travel clockwise around the knot from the top loop, finishing with the Thread Returning.
intention: Three loops, one heart, no end and no beginning; may the threads of my luck run clear and strong.
bestTime: St. Patrick's Day evening (March 17), or any quiet night in March when you want to reflect on how your blessings connect.

name: Easter Egg: The Painted Shell
description: A seven-card spring spread laid in the shape of an egg, with six cards for the painted shell and one golden yolk hidden inside. The shell shows the colours you show the world and the protection around you, while the yolk reveals the new life quietly forming within. Read it at Easter, or on any spring morning when you sense something new about to hatch; it is a warm fit for Ostara-keeping witches too.

positions.name: The Crown of the Shell
positions.meaning: The highest hope or spiritual message painted at the top of your spring.
positions.guide: Look at the very top of your egg. What hope do you want painted brightest on your season?

positions.name: The Left Brushstroke
positions.meaning: The colours of your past that still show on the shell.
positions.guide: Notice the colours here. Which part of your past still shows on your shell, and do you want to keep it?

positions.name: The Right Brushstroke
positions.meaning: The new colour you are adding to your life this spring.
positions.guide: Pick up an imaginary brush. What fresh colour does this card invite you to add to your life?

positions.name: The Shell's Strength
positions.meaning: What protects the new life in you while it is still fragile.
positions.guide: Run your thumb along this card like an eggshell. What keeps you safe while you are still growing?

positions.name: The Golden Yolk
positions.meaning: The new life, idea or self forming quietly inside you.
positions.guide: This is the heart of the egg. What new part of you is quietly forming, and what does it need to grow?

positions.name: The Hairline Crack
positions.meaning: The first sign of change, the place where the shell is ready to give.
positions.guide: Every hatching starts with a tiny crack. Where is your life ready to open, and can you let it?

positions.name: The Hatching
positions.meaning: What emerges when the egg finally opens and the new thing steps into the light.
positions.guide: Picture the shell falling away. What steps out into the light, and how will you welcome it?

howToUse: Shuffle with a painted or hard-boiled egg, a flower or a bowl of seeds beside you, breathing in the feeling of spring. Lay the Crown of the Shell at the top, the two Brushstrokes on the row below, then the Shell's Strength, the Golden Yolk and the Hairline Crack across the widest row. Place the Hatching at the bottom to round off the egg. Read the shell around its edge from the crown downward, then turn to the Golden Yolk at the centre, and finish with the Hatching.
intention: Inside this shell, new life is stirring; I keep it safe, I paint it bright, and I welcome what hatches.
bestTime: Easter Sunday morning, or any spring morning around the vernal equinox and Easter.

name: Easter Egg Hunt: Hidden Gifts
description: A playful four-card Easter spread for finding the gifts tucked away in your life, like eggs hidden in the garden. Three cards are eggs hidden in different places, and the basket shows what you carry home once they are found. Perfect for Easter weekend, a spring picnic or any day you need reminding that good things are hidden all around you.

positions.name: The Egg Under the Hedge
positions.meaning: A gift hidden in your everyday routine that you keep walking past.
positions.guide: Get down low and look under the hedge. Which ordinary moment in your day holds a treat you have overlooked?

positions.name: The Egg in the Tall Grass
positions.meaning: A strength or talent of yours that has grown over and needs uncovering.
positions.guide: Part the grass around this card. What talent of yours has been hidden too long, and how can you use it?

positions.name: The Egg by the Garden Gate
positions.meaning: A gift or opportunity arriving through another person or a new opening.
positions.guide: Peek through the gate. Who or what is bringing you a gift, and are you ready to open the latch?

positions.name: The Brimming Basket
positions.meaning: What you gather and carry home once all the hidden gifts are found.
positions.guide: Lift your full basket. What will you do with everything you found, and who will you share it with?

howToUse: Shuffle while thinking of a garden in spring, or hide three small treats around the room and find them first. Lay the Egg Under the Hedge on the left, the Egg in the Tall Grass a little higher in the middle and the Egg by the Garden Gate on the right. Set the Brimming Basket below the middle egg. Read the eggs from left to right, as if hunting across the garden, then finish with the basket.
intention: Good things are hidden all around me; I look with curious eyes and gather every gift.
bestTime: Easter weekend, especially Easter Sunday, or any bright spring afternoon in March or April.

name: The Spring Hare at Dawn
description: A six-card Easter and springtime spread laid in the shape of a hare, the swift and lucky creature that has long danced through spring fields and folk stories. Its long ears listen, its heart races, its paws keep it grounded, and its strong hind leg shows where to leap. Read it at Easter or through the spring season when you need to know whether to wait, listen or jump.

positions.name: The Listening Ear
positions.meaning: What you are hearing from the world around you: news, signs and other people's voices.
positions.guide: Turn this ear outward. What sounds or messages from others do you need to listen to more closely?

positions.name: The Inward Ear
positions.meaning: What your own inner voice and intuition are telling you.
positions.guide: Turn this ear inward. What is your intuition saying that you have not yet said out loud?

positions.name: The Hare's Bright Eye
positions.meaning: How clearly you are seeing your situation this spring.
positions.guide: Look through the hare's eye. What do you see clearly now, and what is still at the edge of your vision?

positions.name: The Racing Heart
positions.meaning: What excites, frightens or quickens you as the season turns.
positions.guide: Feel your pulse while reading this card. Is your heart racing with excitement, nerves or both?

positions.name: The Grounded Forepaws
positions.meaning: What keeps you steady and still when you need to pause.
positions.guide: Press your palms to the floor. What keeps you steady when it is wiser to sit still and wait?

positions.name: The Leaping Hind Leg
positions.meaning: Where and when to spring forward with all your strength.
positions.guide: Feel the coiled strength in this card. Where should you leap, and what tells you the moment is right?

howToUse: Shuffle at sunrise if you can, with a window open to the morning air, imagining a hare sitting up in a dewy field. Lay the Listening Ear and the Inward Ear side by side at the top, then place the Hare's Bright Eye below them, the Racing Heart below that and the Grounded Forepaws at the bottom. Tuck the Leaping Hind Leg to the right of the heart and paws. Read the ears first, then travel down the body, and finish with the hind leg for your next move.
intention: Swift hare of springtime, lend me your ears to listen, your stillness to wait and your strength to leap.
bestTime: Easter morning at dawn, or any early spring sunrise between the equinox and May.

name: Thanksgiving Cornucopia: Horn of Plenty
description: A seven-card Thanksgiving spread shaped like a cornucopia, the curling horn of plenty spilling over with harvest goods. The horn traces how your abundance has gathered, from its narrow tip to its wide open mouth, and the spilled harvest shows what is overflowing to be shared. Read it during Thanksgiving week to count your blessings and see where plenty flows next.

positions.name: The Curled Tip
positions.meaning: The small beginning or humble seed from which your current plenty grew.
positions.guide: Go back to the very tip of the horn. What small beginning grew into the abundance you have now?

positions.name: The Widening Horn
positions.meaning: The effort and support that helped your blessings grow.
positions.guide: Follow the horn as it widens. Whose help or which effort of yours made your harvest bigger?

positions.name: The Woven Rim
positions.meaning: What holds your abundance together and keeps it from slipping away.
positions.guide: Feel the weave of this card. What habit or value holds your blessings together so they do not slip away?

positions.name: The Open Mouth
positions.meaning: Your capacity to receive: how open you are to the plenty arriving now.
positions.guide: Is your horn open wide or half-closed? What would help you receive good things without guilt?

positions.name: The Spilled Apples
positions.meaning: The everyday blessings tumbling out that you may have taken for granted.
positions.guide: Pick up each apple in your mind. Which simple, daily blessing deserves a proper thank you today?

positions.name: The Gourd and the Grain
positions.meaning: The lasting nourishment that will carry you through the colder months.
positions.guide: Think of food stored for winter. What in this card will keep feeding you long after the feast?

positions.name: The Overflowing Share
positions.meaning: What you have in excess and are called to give to others.
positions.guide: Your horn is overflowing. What can you share this season, and who would be glad to receive it?

howToUse: Shuffle with a bowl of fruit, nuts or a few dried leaves on the table, saying thank you for one thing with each cut of the deck. Lay the Curled Tip at the top right, then curve down and to the left with the Widening Horn, the Woven Rim and the Open Mouth, so the horn opens toward the lower left. Spill the last three cards along the bottom: the Spilled Apples, the Gourd and the Grain, and the Overflowing Share. Read the horn from tip to mouth, then read the spilled harvest from left to right.
intention: My horn is full and my heart is fuller; I give thanks for all I have and share what overflows.
bestTime: Thanksgiving week, especially Thanksgiving Day itself (the fourth Thursday in November in the US, the second Monday in October in Canada), or any late autumn evening.

name: Thanksgiving: The Gratitude Table
description: A seven-card Thanksgiving spread laid out like a long feast table, with a host at the head, guests along both sides, a centrepiece in the middle and an empty chair at the foot. It is a reading about the people, gifts and memories that nourish you, and about who and what you are making room for. Lay it during Thanksgiving week, before or after the feast, as a quiet ritual of thanks.

positions.name: The Head of the Table
positions.meaning: The role you play in your circle right now, as host, guest or keeper of the feast.
positions.guide: Take your seat at the head. Are you the one hosting, serving or being served, and how does that feel?

positions.name: The Guest Who Feeds You
positions.meaning: A person or presence who nourishes you and deserves your thanks.
positions.guide: Look across the table at this card. Who nourishes you, and how will you thank them this week?

positions.name: The Seat of Old Memories
positions.meaning: A memory, tradition or departed loved one still present at your table.
positions.guide: Pull out this chair for someone or something from the past. What tradition or loved one still sits with you?

positions.name: The Guest Who Challenges
positions.meaning: The difficult relationship or tension at the table that asks for patience.
positions.guide: Every table has a tricky guest. What tension does this card show, and how can you meet it with grace?

positions.name: The Unspoken Grace
positions.meaning: The thanks you feel but have not yet said aloud.
positions.guide: What gratitude is sitting on your tongue unspoken? Practise saying it while you look at this card.

positions.name: The Harvest Centrepiece
positions.meaning: The shared blessing at the heart of your circle that everyone gathers around.
positions.guide: This is what everyone gathers around. What shared blessing holds your circle together this year?

positions.name: The Empty Chair
positions.meaning: Who or what you are making room for in the year ahead.
positions.guide: Look at the empty chair at the foot of the table. Who or what are you making room for next?

howToUse: Shuffle at your own table if you can, with a candle lit and a cup of something warm, naming one person you are grateful for. Lay the Head of the Table at the top, then set the guests down both sides: the Guest Who Feeds You and the Seat of Old Memories on the left, the Guest Who Challenges and the Unspoken Grace on the right. Place the Harvest Centrepiece in the middle of the table and the Empty Chair at the bottom, at the foot. Read the head first, then the left side, the right side and the centrepiece, and finish at the Empty Chair.
intention: I set a table of thanks for those who feed me, those who test me and those I remember; there is always room for one more.
bestTime: Thanksgiving Day or the evening before (the fourth Thursday in November in the US, the second Monday in October in Canada), or any shared meal in late autumn.

name: Thanksgiving Wishbone
description: A simple three-card Thanksgiving spread inspired by the old custom of two people pulling a wishbone after the feast. One prong holds what you are thankful for, the other what you are ready to let go, and the joint where they meet reveals the wish that snaps free. Quick enough to do at the table after dinner, and lovely to share with a friend.

positions.name: The Thankful Prong
positions.meaning: What you are grateful for and want to hold onto.
positions.guide: Grip this side of the wishbone. What are you most grateful for this year, and how will you keep it close?

positions.name: The Letting-Go Prong
positions.meaning: What you are ready to release as the year winds down.
positions.guide: Feel this side loosen in your hand. What are you ready to let go of before the year ends?

positions.name: The Wish That Snaps Free
positions.meaning: The wish or blessing that comes to you when gratitude and release meet.
positions.guide: Hear the snap. What wish rises in you now, and what is one small step to help it come true?

howToUse: Shuffle after the feast, ideally with the wishbone itself (or a twig) on the table and a friend to pull it with. Lay the Thankful Prong at the top left and the Letting-Go Prong at the top right, then place the Wish That Snaps Free below and between them, where the two prongs join. Read the thankful prong first, then the letting-go prong, and finish with the wish.
intention: With thanks in one hand and release in the other, I pull, I let go, and my wish breaks free.
bestTime: Thanksgiving night after dinner, or any evening of late autumn harvest gatherings.
